title: Add a Land cleanup stage that tears down task-created runtime resources
description:
User request: add a dedicated cleanup stage to Land that tears down processes, UIs, sockets and other temporary resources created during the work: “leave the campsite how you found it”.

The CPU observation on 16 October 2026 found five long-lived Storybook servers retaining approximately 4.04 GiB of process footprint, mostly compressed, plus several older UI servers. Process teardown is not currently an explicit Land stage: .workflows/land/workflow.ts has worktree cleanup within verify, followed by local-update, publish and report. Removing a checkout does not prove that its servers, watchers, process trees or sockets have been torn down.

Scope: introduce an explicit, inspectable cleanup stage and retain enough resource provenance to clean up the whole task, including implementation, delegated work, tests, browser/UI previews and local installation smoke checks, rather than only processes started after Land begins. Cover task-created servers/UIs, background commands and watchers, descendants, listening ports, Unix sockets and associated temporary resources. Coordinate stage ordering so cleanup still has ownership evidence if feature worktrees have already been removed, and so checks/smoke tests cannot leave new resources after the final cleanup gate.

Restore the starting environment: preserve pre-existing/shared services, unrelated sessions/worktrees, the canonical checkout and permanent selected BEADS_DB. An intentional persistent result must be explicitly requested and recorded; unowned resources must be reported for resolution instead of broad process-name/path killing. Existing source/worktree cleanup and Busy Bee completion/publication authority must remain coherent.

Pointers: .workflows/land/workflow.ts; lib/busybee/tests/integration/land.test.ts; docs/busybee-workflows.md; lib/busybee/SPEC.md; docs/agents/specialists.md; docs/architecture.md. Measurement evidence: /Users/ct/.config/codex/visualizations/2026/10/16/01a14334-f4f8-7090-9ff7-3937cb42fcdb/cpu-qlock-report.html and cpu-qlock-evidence.json. Obtain librarian guidance on ownership and lifecycle boundaries before implementation, and bookworm coverage for workflow instructions/documentation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Land exposes a distinct cleanup stage in its state chart, generated stage brief and workflow projection; successful completion requires cleanup evidence.
2. The task retains or recovers resource ownership/baseline evidence spanning implementation and delegated work through final verification/smoke checks, even when a feature worktree has been removed.
3. Before successful completion, task-created temporary process trees, UI/Storybook servers, watchers, listeners/sockets and temporary resources are shut down or removed and their absence is verified. Deliberately retained user-requested resources have an explicit disposition.
4. Pre-existing/shared/unrelated resources, canonical checkout and permanent tracker are preserved. Ambiguous ownership or failed teardown remains visible with the exact resource and next action; cleanup cannot silently pass.
5. Focused coverage exercises successful cleanup, resource ownership/isolation, retry/resume or partial teardown, and failure preventing completion. Relevant workflow checks and the complete repository check pass.

title: Bee librarian: hv-lqeh.7
description:
{"cwd":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/fix--beads-host-sync","effort":"xhigh","harness":"codex","kind":"librarian","model":"gpt-6-astra","prompt":"","system_prompt":"When launched by Colony, follow its execution runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and publish the updates. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish. Return the evidence ID and publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

Interpretation — hv-9uery.1 and its coordinator update supply the request (paraphrase, not a direct user transcript): compare direct+optional workflows with workflow-only/default do-work; no production defaults, unlimited retries or landing. Difficulty is that Colony's fixed related-task admission/claim set and Busy Bee's dynamic per-visit work have different lifetimes. Native closure, accepted workflow result and completed request are separate facts.

Resolution — existing intent is XState/Busy Bee progression, native work, Colony execution/claims and bounded retries. Librarian proposes the ordinary task run as the single outer completion anchor, closed only by Busy Bee on done. Compose public commands first: caller JSON -> one run -> explicit open/unassigned handoff -> Bee driver -> claim initial unassigned manual visit -> persist result, close visit, next/choice -> done. Resume the existing run, never initialize on every attempt. This is advice, not accepted product policy. Automatic visits keep their independent Bee requests and require collect plus explicit outer blocked propagation. No cross-product imports or Colony checkpoint duplication.

Guidance gap — missing concrete handoff guidance at the integration seam, not a violation of either package's documented ownership. An in_progress run is excluded by native ready; the first manual visit does not follow later run reassignment. Same-request automatic attempts preserve identity, while explicit bee retry mints a new identity and does not transfer existing manual visits. Colony releases only recorded related-task claims. Original caller tasks are not reused as Busy Bee visits automatically. Input worktree data does not set Bee cwd. These distinctions need evidence before production interface choices.

Fixture removed. Recommend a minimal manual-stage comparison, durable pre-close result for close/submit interruption, explicit stopped-predecessor handoff for new identities, and counts including run/checkpoint/visit/spawn plus any pre-existing tasks. Automatic nested drivers also need child-block handling, available capacity and protection from recursive implicit workflow wrapping; no new recovery machinery proposed. partial_effects/checkpoint_locked remains an explicit blocker, not license to steal locks. title: Architecture evidence: local CLI artifacts and runtime ownership
description:

- **Interpretation** — hv-f7fl0 supplies ct's request as a task description rather than a verbatim conversation: real local builds, separate explicit global installation, native compilation where practical, no live launcher replacement during verification. The difficult distinction is bundling product code versus retaining filesystem-owned runtime inputs. Baseline installers write checkout launchers; Colony uses process.execPath plus source paths, which cannot be carried unchanged into standalone binaries.
- **Resolution** — Librarian proposal, adoption pending: package-local dist/<command> with direct host Bun compilation, installation through one Tooling command called by package scripts, stage/copy/chmod/rename in the destination filesystem. No product imports from Tooling and no Shared installer API. Colony owns the source/compiled entry resolver and adjacent colony-runtime/colony-worker/colony-watchdog companions, plus bee and colony; use explicit standalone detection, not missing-file fallbacks. Resolve post-run prompt CLI paths through the same contract. Busy Bee keeps dynamic absolute filesystem imports and needs explicit compiled configuration autoload for checkout dependencies; Waggle keeps caller-relative or explicit classifier files. Include existing foreground hive-ui as a public executable; compile its HTML graph using a small package-local Bun.build script with bun-plugin-tailwind. Do not invent Shared/Tooling product CLIs. Exact layout/interface are proposals; package independence and caller-owned catalogues are established intent.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and record the updates locally. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

title: Evaluate three fixes for Beads sync conflicts with isolated spikes
description: ct requests a report after upstream Beads Rust and Beads Viewer investigations, with exactly three potential approaches ranked by correctness and ease of implementation. Validate key assumptions with isolated spikes before presenting. Inputs: report tasks hv-ypbh and hv-gs30, five saved recovery snapshot triplets under /tmp/hive-tracker-recovery-20261010, reproduced comment/timestamp/comment-ID conflicts, Colony dispatch failure events. Scope: disposable isolated fixtures and spike code in a nested Honeycomb worktree; no production policy changes, tracker repairs or deployment. Compare comment preservation, genuine claim/state conflicts, cross-clone versus local coordination, pending native merge receipts, behavior of Viewer, operational complexity and limitations. Deliver evidence-backed recommendation and concise three-option comparison. Preserve useful spike artifacts for review. User is away; proceed autonomously within scope.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly three concrete approaches compared by correctness and effort; independent upstream research incorporated; key assumptions exercised with isolated native or pure spikes and results documented; recommended next step and limitations explicit; live tracker and production application behavior unchanged.
notes:
Worktree: /Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/codex--beads-sync-options-spikes. Research tasks hv-ypbh and hv-gs30 are executing. Plan: reproduce baseline conflicts, exercise native br merge on saved and synthetic isolated snapshots, prototype a narrow comments-only normalization/union route, and evaluate coordination boundaries. No production code or real tracker recovery changes.
Native br 0.7.4 isolated spike complete: preserves both appended comments even with colliding local comment IDs and comment-ID renumbering; refuses competing claims and disputed titles. On saved batches it resolves second/third/fifth with zero missing comments, but initial/fourth remain conflicting because two sides recorded different scalar closed_at values for the same completed outcome. Artifacts: spikes/beads-sync/native_spike.py and native-results.json in worktree. No force flags used; all fixtures disposable and isolated from real BEADS_DB.
All three spikes now run: native reconciliation, conservative custom comments merge, and authority coordination. Native and narrow prototype resolve exactly 3/5 saved batches; both retain initial/fourth conflicts on different closed_at scalar values. Both preserve comments and reject competing claims/title disputes. Narrow prototype commutativity verified for all 9 cases. Authority spike: shared DB rejects stale guarded claim (exit 6, first assignee preserved); duplicate closure skips (NOTHING_TO_DO exit 3, original closed_at retained); independent DBs closing same row produce different closed_at and merge conflict; br writer succeeds with .hive-sync.lock directory present. Artifacts under spikes/beads-sync. These support one authority plus native reconciliation as structural option, native semantic transport adapter as pragmatic option, or narrow existing-driver correction as easiest limited option. Coordination spike does not prove distributed leasing or full publication exclusion.
Historical dispatch.rank provenance established: before f8af6e7 (Oct 8 22:41:33 BST / 21:41 UTC), pageRanks copied live SQLite including pending sync receipt to a disposable DB then called br sync --flush-only on that copy before BV. A database_committed receipt in that copy explains mutation refusal at dispatch.rank without BV itself syncing. f8af6e7 already replaced this with direct bv --db live database. Current ranking smoke fixture explicitly covers pending receipt read-without-mutation. This is a historical integration problem already fixed, separate from current Git driver conflicts. Source verified via git show 2f1ed8b and 60ddfac ranking.ts plus f8af6e7.

In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and record the updates locally. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships. Publish only at the root runbook’s explicit remote-exchange checkpoints. Return the evidence ID and local/publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Record authorized Beads updates locally and follow the existing runbook’s publication checkpoints; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

comments.text:
Consultation complete. Recommendation is a proposal; no policy or implementation change is approved by this report. Architectural evidence: hv-ktovc (topic repository-command-discovery-ownership).

Use mise as a small, described repository-task catalog, with Bun scripts retaining executable recipes. This best addresses the stated discovery problem while reusing working callers. The value is fewer command catalogs in agent context, not fewer package.json keys.

| Surface | Responsibility and concrete candidates |
| --- | --- |
| package.json | Package/lifecycle primitives and shared execution recipes. Keep workspace typecheck, build/install:bin, Honeycomb schema scripts, root typecheck/test:all/check, and prepare. Exact flags and check composition live here once. |
| mise.toml | Repository environment, setup and a curated discovery menu. Describe existing default; candidate entries are check, test:changed, fmt, beads:sync and UI start/dev. Delegate to Bun recipes; UI entries can call its package-local start/dev directly, making root ui/ui:dev aliases removal candidates after updating their callers. Do not mirror all 18 scripts. |
| Skills and AGENTS | Skills explain when to choose focused tests, changed tests or the final gate, and how to interpret results. AGENTS retains mandatory verification/publication timing and a short discovery pointer. Keep one canonical invocation at the relevant decision; remove repeated command inventories/flag explanations if the proposal is adopted. |
| Hooks | Own event timing: prepare/install, Git validation and harness environment initialization. Call the same underlying recipes as manual callers. |
| Product CLIs | Own domain behavior, flags and help. waggle/busybee root launchers are checkout conveniences; retain them where useful without reproducing their subcommands in mise or skills. Repository-maintenance implementations remain in lib/tooling. |

Caller constraints grounded in current source:

- .husky/pre-commit invokes root typecheck; pre-merge-commit invokes pre-commit. Root check shares typecheck. Keep this reuse. package.json also filters Honeycomb schema:stage from lint-staged; workspace filtering is meaningful.
- test-changed.ts:21-35 invokes root test:all to share timeout/parallelism defaults. Preserve that single recipe. A mise wrapper must forward test arguments and preserve exit/output behavior.
- prepare invokes git:setup and beads-setup-auto; default mise setup orders install, workspace build, workspace install:bin, then beads:bootstrap. Keep lifecycle/setup helpers in Bun and preserve ordering. Mise dependency arrays do not imply sequence.
- Pi session_start calls bun run beads:env --json and parses stdout. Claude calls beads-hook.ts directly. Both reach beads-environment.ts/mise env. Keep machine environment resolution separate from the discovery menu; descriptions belong outside JSON stdout.
- beads:sync is an explicit actor publication step in the runbook. A catalog entry changes discoverability only; it must not move publication into prepare, Git hooks or session hooks. Existing lock requirements still apply to execution.

Alternative: keep ordinary commands in Bun and use mise chiefly for setup/environment/daemon configuration. This is the least-change option and works with concise guidance, but provides a weaker described task menu. The curated option adds a small public discovery surface; it earns that cost only when it replaces repeated menus. Avoid changing caller spelling merely for uniformity. ct's unresolved decision is which everyday entry point to adopt; no further investigation is needed to complete this consultation.

Evidence/reuse: inspected clean revision 77bb3d70a65542a1ba22e7046efa5da44add742d, root manifests/hooks, named harness callers, involved tooling helpers, workspace manifests, architecture and testing/land guidance. Official [mise tasks](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/) supports descriptions/listing; [usage specifications](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/running-tasks.html) supply argument help; [Bun filtering](https://bun.sh/docs/pm/filter) preserves workspace selection. Existing architecture assigns maintenance to Tooling and domain behavior to product CLIs; it does not currently choose Bun versus mise for repository discovery.

Verification: source/caller inspection only; git status --porcelain=v1 remained empty and HEAD unchanged. No examined source, architecture documentation or implementation task was changed. No quality suites or speculative replacement commands were run; this report validates a responsibility proposal, not migration behavior. You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and record the updates locally. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships. Publish only at the root runbook’s explicit remote-exchange checkpoints. Return the evidence ID and local/publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.

## Current direction and delivery order — 2026-10-04

Current outcome summary: hv-3x8.9.1 design. Verbatim evidence: hv-3x8.17. Next implementation: hv-3x8.9.3.

The daemon hosts repository-specific colonies (event loops); a sleeping colony does not poll, launch, retry or reconcile. Bee creates requests in Beads independently. A recipe snapshots chosen request parameters; Colony selects the current formula by harness name to produce the actual invocation. Both use canonical bees.toml for their respective concerns. Bee permits per-request CLI values but no alternate recipe file; Colony's transient overrides change formulas/limits, not recipes. SQLite retains registry and formula/override/dispatch history; each wake re-reads canonical config. Use wake/sleep, tmux-style lazy server startup, explicit registration operations, and optional temporary activation. No min policy, no model-cost inference, no idle auto-expiry. Full details and open issues live in hv-3x8.9.1, not in earlier brainstorming below.

NEXT is hv-3x8.9.3: launch a bee from a manually created spawn bead via a small Colony CLI command. Define that slice's cli.ts interface first, then build its usable runtime path. No daemon, Bee CLI or all-commands skeleton yet. This explicit user sequencing replaces the earlier spec -> rename -> shared -> Bee -> daemon waterfall as a prerequisite for the first slice. The full specification and package alignment remain valuable follow-ups, not required detours before this first vertical proof.

The older claim that every request must already come through a implemented Bee producer does not prohibit the approved manual br fixture. Colony remains the execution consumer, not a bypass around spawn beads. Future producer/shared/spec work must reuse the first slice's proven contract. Existing identity, harness capability scope and user-fork exclusions remain unchanged.

Current repository rules allow product imports through @hive/shared only; no mandatory colony -> bee import is needed by the new recipe/formula boundary. Do not silently implement that older proposed exception. GLOSSARY.md and older docs need subsequent reconciliation to the daemon/colony and recipe/formula vocabulary; their update is tracked rather than falsely claimed here.

## Historical prior scope — superseded where inconsistent above

Give coding agents friendly names for identity attribution in Beads, and build a mechanism for human or agent requesters to ask Colony to run bees across harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Pi). These are planned capabilities, not implemented runtime support.

Current vocabulary follows GLOSSARY.md (refined in hv-yan, landed at 882ab2d). Identity identifies a human or agent; best-effort agent attributes describe execution. Owner is the accountable human, distinct from Assignee and Actor. A bee is a running agent, not its request. AFK (away-from-keyboard) work after human-agent planning is the intended default bee mode; HITL (human-in-the-loop) work involves ongoing human participation. This is a terminology alignment, not a new scheduling policy or lifecycle enum.

Three orthogonal parts, sharing only a contract in @hive/shared:
- scent: identity plugins for harnesses (Claude/Codex SessionStart hooks, Pi extension). Reads harness event/context and inherited env; mints a friendly name when no identity is supplied; exports BD_ACTOR (friendly name), BR_HARNESS, BR_MODEL, BR_AGENT_NAME where the harness allows env injection; injects identity into the system prompt/context.
- bee: module + thin CLI. `bee spawn <kind> <task-id>...` creates a spawn bead; `bee status <spawn-id>` reads it. Bee kinds live in a repo-root bees.toml.
- colony: one system-wide daemon (renamed from ghost) that watches spawn beads, launches harness CLIs with identity env, supports restarting execution and stopping running bees as determined by the pending lifecycle design. Only allowed cross-package import: colony -> bee.
An agent can have an identity without being a bee, and a bee is attributed through its inherited env even without scent.

Recorded design inputs (full rationale in the transcript record child bead). The behaviors below come from earlier decisions; final bee lifecycle states, transitions and outcome/event names remain work for hv-3x8.9.1 and hv-3x8.12. The retired term "reap" is not a current domain operation or agreed enum value:
- Friendly name: 3-word adjective-adjective-noun, deterministic from session id for sessions started directly; minted at admission for bees. Model/effort are best-effort agent attributes, separate from identity.
- Identity resolution in scent is lifecycle-aware: sessions started directly mint from the actual session key; harness subagents use a distinct harness-provided agent key; supplied bee identity is adopted and retained across respawns. Clear/new replaces owned session bindings and prompt state, resume restores the target session identity, and compact retains it. A changed session ID alone does not identify a separately launched agent or the requester of a bee; Hive does not add an agent parent-child hierarchy.
- A spawn bead records a request for a bee to work on specified task beads (linked with related deps); it is distinct from the running bee and from the work itself. One request may reference several task beads. Its Requester is the human or agent identity credited with requesting it, not a parent or lifecycle owner. Labels: system, bee, agent:<kind>. br label filters are exact-match, so system:bee would NOT be hidden by --exclude-label system (verified); ordinary agent work already excludes `system` and must ignore system beads.
- bees.toml `users = [...]` is a configurable list of human names (e.g. ct); `bee spawn` fails loudly if any task is assigned to one.
- No single-instance lock for colony.
- Attribution fields: BR_HARNESS=<harness> (e.g. claude) and BR_AGENT_NAME=<bee kind> (e.g. scout), never combined.
- Launch rule: all linked tasks must be ready. A bad DAG is a mistake to fix, not to work around; blocked tasks are allowed at spawn time (deferring a DAG is essential).
- All bee requests go through the bee tool and Colony; no direct subprocess launch path. A requesting agent waiting for requested work is informed via `bee status`, not protected from scheduling waits. This does not describe a parent-child relationship or prohibit harness subagents.
- The earlier design calls for closing a spawn bead to end its request and stop any running bee (allowing interactive TUI bees later). Closed linked tasks count as satisfied: the launch rule applies to the open ones, and Colony closes a request without launching only when all its tasks are closed. A bee whose task claim fails closes its own spawn bead (encoded in the bee policy prompt). Crashes respawn up to max_retries; then colony closes the spawn bead and forcefully returns the bee's claimed tasks to open, as it does after ending a request with unfinished claimed work. colony logs to its own log, not the bead, and emits tracked events for lifecycle actions (likely JSONL).
- colony restarts are likely (e.g. upgrades): bees run detached and survive them; colony recovers from tracked pids and/or a scan of spawn beads.
- Harness subagent definitions (.codex/agents, .pi/agents, agents:sync) are dropped in favour of bees, not regenerated from bees.toml. scripts/beads-loop.ts is temporary and not a design constraint.
- Supersedes the actor policy from hv-ri0 (actor = harness name).

Ordering: spikes and GLOSSARY.md first; then the colony design (hv-3x8.9.1) and the spec (hv-3x8.12), which is the living reference for all later work; then rename, shared contract, scent, bee, colony, retirement.

Claude Code harness subagents (Agent/Task) are supported in the planned identity system through the same explicit-attribution approach as Codex. This supersedes the brief exclusion recorded earlier in this discussion.

- Pi: process environment plus stable composable identity in the system prompt on each run.

- Codex sessions started directly, Codex harness subagents and Claude Code harness subagents: identity context with explicit `br --actor <own-friendly-name>` on every tracker mutation. Share the explicit-attribution guidance; keep event parsing and context delivery in the harness-specific adapters.

The final policy is agreed here; end-to-end harness subagent attribution is an implementation acceptance criterion, not a completed runtime result of the original spike. The agreed MVP lifecycle boundary is recorded in docs/agent-identity-scope.md: clear/new, resume and compact are supported; user forks are excluded.

MVP supports start, clear/new, resume, compact and harness-subagent attribution. User fork-in-session and new-fork flows, cache-preserving identity migration and generic GUI support are intentionally excluded. Harness subagents remain in scope even when their harness internally copies history.

title: Spike: br database discovery across nested worktrees and BEADS_DB policy
description:
Before bee and colony pin which Beads database a bee uses, establish how br behaves when invoked from nested Git worktrees (honeycomb creates them under .worktrees/ in this repo).

Questions:
- From a nested worktree cwd, which .beads/ does br discover: the worktree's checked-out copy or the main checkout's? Is the SQLite db shared or per worktree, and how does the Husky reconciliation (pre-commit / post-merge / post-checkout) interact?
- If a bee mutates beads from a worktree while colony reads the main checkout, when does each side see the change?
- Does forcing BEADS_DB (br honours the env var and --db) to the canonical git-root database work from a worktree, and what breaks (auto-flush to JSONL, freshness checks, --allow-stale)?
- colony is one system-wide daemon serving many repos (not started per repo): how should it address each repo's database when polling spawn beads and launching bees?
- Recommend a policy: bee caller's cwd vs BEADS_DB always = canonical git root. ct leans to the bee caller's cwd, and is open to a policy change making BEADS_DB always the canonical git root if the spike shows it is needed (hv-3x8.11 turn 7 #5).

Prior evidence: hv-mmk and hv-00n verified two-worktree reconciliation. Use disposable repos/worktrees in $TMPDIR; do not mutate this repo's tracker for experiments.
design: Research-only spike; no product or repo-policy edits. Use isolated HOME/XDG/Git config and disposable repos under TMPDIR. Compare default br discovery/visibility with Hive no-auto-import/no-auto-flush config; run copied reconciliation hooks through real Git lifecycle; test BEADS_DB and --db from nested worktrees, freshness guards and ambient overrides. Record exact reproducible commands, outcomes, recommended bee/colony routing and follow-ups on this bead only. Baseline bun run check passed in task worktree.
