title: AFK prototype: build Bee and Colony end to end
description:
# Independent AFK prototype: build Bee and Colony end to end

## Mandate and isolation

This is a parallel, experimental build epic authorized by ct after the 2026-10-04 architecture grilling. Build a working prototype start-to-finish in an autonomous agent loop; it might be suitable to ship, but shipping is not assumed. This is NOT another design/HITL phase. The agent is delegated ordinary implementation choices, command naming, small schema decisions and prototype tradeoffs. Make a concrete choice, record it with evidence, and keep progressing rather than asking ct to bikeshed every detail.

The original hv-3x8 epic and ALL its descendants are read-only reference material. Do not claim, update, close, reparent, relabel or add dependency/related edges to those records. This prototype has its own top-level epic, features and implementation tasks and no prerequisite on the original plan. Read the current section of hv-3x8.9.1 and the source dialogue hv-3x8.17 as context only; this epic freezes the prototype contract and explicitly supplies defaults for previously open questions. Do not replay superseded proposals from the transcript. Do not treat success here as completing the original epic.

Use a dedicated nested Honeycomb worktree and prototype branch. Implement in sensible existing/new package locations after consulting the librarian; do not dump a second application into scripts or invent a parallel framework. Preserve current only-@hive/shared cross-package boundaries. Changes to main, production services, installed user harness configuration or original tracker work are not part of this authorization. The prototype may alter code in its isolated branch, but must not retire the existing worker loop, native agent definitions or hooks merely because the original plan contemplated that later. No automatic merge, release, Homebrew publication or deployment.

Scope is the complete Bee/Colony request/configuration/dispatch/daemon/scheduling/recovery/inspection path, including launcher-provided identity and native harness launch profiles. Standalone Scent/native-session hook rollout is orthogonal and remains out of scope; supplied identity must work without it. No GUI, cron service, model-price accounting, minimum worker population, compatibility shims or speculative capability/plugin framework.

## Mandatory build style: useful vertical slices and libraries

1. Work in small usable slices. The first launches one bee from a manually created spawn bead with no daemon or Bee CLI. For each slice define its cli.ts command/flag/help/JSON surface before implementing that path. Do not first scaffold the entire CLI, all packages, all types or a universal service framework.
2. Lean on maintained libraries where they fit. Consult current authoritative docs and existing repo patterns before building equivalent machinery. Commander for command parsing, existing schemas/Zod, Bun.TOML and Bun SQLite are natural starting points; use the repo's existing tools where appropriate. An ORM is not mandatory merely because there is SQLite.
3. As soon as there are multiple meaningful discriminated unions to branch over, use ts-pattern for exhaustive matching. Do not accumulate parallel switch ladders or avoid the library through casts and optional fields. This prototype will cross that threshold in its request/command/launch results, so adopt it in the first meaningful contracts, not as a later cleanup promise.
4. As soon as lifecycle/state transitions exceed a couple of simple cases, use XState. This prototype's awake/asleep plus request/attempt/retry/recovery behavior crosses that threshold. Introduce an actual XState model with the daemon/lifecycle slice rather than a growing collection of booleans, timers and ad hoc transition reducers. A token import or a dead demonstration machine does not satisfy this directive.
5. Use a popular existing template engine and its normal language, not handwritten substitution or a new DSL. Handlebars is the researched default candidate: strict missing values, no HTML escaping for argv, eager syntax validation at config load because compile() is lazy. Verify its current documented API and a tiny runtime probe; another established tool is acceptable if a concrete mismatch warrants it. Execute executable + argument tokens without a shell command string. No unrestricted shell evaluation hidden inside recipe templating.
6. Fail loudly for invalid config, missing named formulas, unsupported invocation parameters and ownership ambiguity. Do not silently invent values, fall back to another model/harness, swallow failures or build a production-grade recovery framework for hypothetical cases.

## Product contract frozen for this prototype

- A system-wide daemon hosts one event loop per registered repository (a colony). A bee is the running agent; its spawn bead is a request. A task bead is the work. Identity/Actor/Owner/Assignee remain distinct.
- Bee reads canonical-root bees.toml recipe/kind defaults, applies explicit recipe flags such as --model, --effort and --harness, and snapshots the effective values in a spawn bead. No alternate Bee --config file, worktree-first lookup or runtime daemon dependency. Bee may submit while server/colony is down or asleep.
- Colony loads canonical configuration on wake and applies the current named harness formula to the captured recipe. Kind defaults and caps are distinct from executable/argv formulas keyed by harness name. Bee may name a harness installed only via a Colony formula override; the two sides do not auto-synchronize.
- Default execution cwd is the canonical worktree. Explicit --cwd may be any existing directory and changes execution location only, not configuration discovery or the selected tracker. Persist explicit per-repository/per-attempt BEADS_DB authority; never route by the daemon's own cwd or mutate global environment when switching repositories.
- Spawn classification is separate exact-match labels system, bee, agent:<kind>, with related task links and supplied/minted friendly assignee. Snapshot recipe data structurally, not as shell strings stuffed into labels. Spawn creation does not claim task beads. Preserve human-reservation and duplicate-open-request refusals; blocked tasks may wait.
- Colony init creates config; wake/sleep control colony activity; explicit add/remove manage registry membership; daemon commands are separate. Use tmux-like lazy default server startup and explicit socket/server targeting. CLI names beyond those meanings may be chosen by the builder and documented.
- Nothing happens in a sleeping colony: no request polling, launch, retry or closure reconciliation. Detached bees continue. On wake reconcile closed requests as well as open ones: do not relaunch a closed request, and stop a known surviving execution whose request closed, then release its unfinished claims.
- Durable awake registrations recover after daemon restart; sleeping registrations stay asleep. wake --temp lasts only until explicit sleep/remove or daemon exit and is not restored. No queue-empty/idle auto-expiry. A fresh wake, including recovery wake, re-reads canonical configuration rather than restoring transient formula/limit overrides.
- Canonical configuration is the durable baseline. Colony SQLite may hold active formula/limit overrides, NOT recipe-default overrides, and immutable history. Reset/wake drops active overrides, not their audit trail. Request values do not change, but a later template can change a retry's actual invocation. Record spawn/recipe identity, actual formula revision, actual executable/argv and attempt outcome; requested/source formula identity is not proof of execution identity.
- Attribution for CLI config changes should reuse explicit actor/environment conventions; do not fabricate who authored a manually edited file. Logs live outside Beads. Minimal last-observed request summaries may be written for Bee status, with timestamps/freshness; do not promise live daemon state from Beads.
- No min. Use non-preemptive per-kind and per-colony maxima, with the scoped execution-location cap below. Reducing 20 to 18 leaves all existing workers alive; new launch eligibility resumes at count 17. Do not infer monetary cost from model names.
- All remaining open linked tasks must be ready; closed tasks satisfy the request. All tasks closed means close request without launching. Highest urgency among related task beads wins capacity (P0 ahead of P1); use existing BV ranking for same-priority work if a complete usable ranking interface can be obtained, not a new homemade graph ranker.
- Crashes can retry within a configured budget. Confirm the old owned execution stopped before clearing its own unfinished task claims; replacement reclaims them using the same spawn-friendly identity. Cancellation/exhaustion closes the request and releases only its own unfinished claims. Do not infer provider success solely from process exit code if the request remains unfinished.

## Concrete AFK defaults for previously open details

These are prototype decisions, not changes to the original epic. The builder may replace a choice when a real smoke demonstrates a problem, provided the reason, changed contract and regression receipt are recorded in this prototype's notes/docs.

- Start with max_retries = 3 additional attempts after the first. Count each unfinished unexpected exit against the budget; no elaborate progress-based reset rule. Select/document a small bounded retry delay through configuration and keep delay tests deterministic. No retries while asleep.
- If a multi-task claim fails, stop that request rather than inventing partial-work scheduling; after its execution stops release only the tasks this execution actually claimed. A task reserved for a human after submission, or claimed by another agent, keeps the request waiting with a visible reason. Never steal or clear someone else's claim.
- Registry membership and wake state are distinct: sleeping durable entries remain discoverable; remove forgets future scheduling but does not delete config/Beads data or kill unrelated processes. Existing owned executions still have their attempt records; the CLI must expose that they can outlive registration. Re-add/wake can reconcile them without duplicate launch.
- Per-worktree capacity uses the worktree containing the recorded launch cwd, or canonicalized external cwd when it is not in a worktree. Capture that bucket at dispatch; do not chase later process chdir or automatically-created worktrees. Canonical-default launches therefore share the canonical bucket. Scope the colony-wide total per registered repository; a server-global budget is not required initially.
- BV investigation must not stall the build. Prefer a verified complete score source for eligible task IDs and aggregate by best ranked linked task within a native-priority tier. Known triage output can be top-10 only. If no complete contract is available, use explicitly documented FIFO (request creation time, then ID) within the priority tier, expose that mode, and retain the limitation in the final report. Do not treat missing BV scores as proof of lowest rank or silently change a configured ranking mode after an error.
- For argv/model/prompt fields, use the chosen library's normal syntax and strict failure behavior. Names/schema details are delegated; no need to ask ct about every spelling. Unknown recipe fields, missing values and invalid configured formulas must have a small explicit boundary contract, not silent guessing.
- Use requested kind labels for caps and actual formula/attempt records for execution history. Select simple final outcome names and a Beads-visible status projection while implementing; do not revive retired reap/ancestry terms from old proposals. Beads-only status describes the request and recorded observations; Colony status inspects the actual runtime.

## Verification: real, small disposable smokes are the main evidence

The user explicitly authorizes small smoke tests against real disposable repositories, SQLite databases, br processes, OS processes and local sockets. This is not permission to use Hive's working tracker or the user's default daemon as test fixtures.

- Create throwaway Git projects and real br/Colony SQLite databases for each scenario, with explicit test endpoints and private socket/state directories. Use a canonical checkout plus linked worktrees for routing tests. The live Hive BEADS_DB remains only for implementation tracking; pass separate explicit endpoint/env to every smoke child so inherited state cannot leak.
- Build only small reusable setup/teardown helpers using existing test patterns. Do not replace br/SQLite/process APIs with giant fake services, and do not create a general-purpose testing framework. Real local scripted harness processes are useful deterministic fixtures but must be identified as fixtures, never claimed as real native-agent conformance.
- Prefer observable CLI outputs, database rows, files, child tool-environment receipts, exit events and log records. Wait on observable conditions with bounded deadlines; avoid arbitrary sleeps, wall-clock races and long monolithic scenarios. Clean up only processes/socket paths/directories owned by the smoke; retain useful failure artifacts and never kill unrelated work.
- Some focused unit tests are appropriate for pure priority/normalization/template boundaries and lifecycle assertions. Do not chase coverage or duplicate schema/library guarantees. Keep slow/provider probes separately selectable from fast unit/integration runs.
- Include a bounded real native-harness launch using already installed tooling/credentials before claiming actual bee-launch conformance. Do not install accounts, change user hook trust, disable production safeguards or run unbounded provider jobs. Missing credentials/binaries are genuine evidenced external blockers, not reasons to fake a pass. Continue independent local slices, leave required unverified acceptance unchecked, and report what is needed.
- Store reproducible commands, fixture setup, outputs and limitations with each task's evidence. Full bun run check plus changed-code/appropriate broader suites are gates; follow the repository's test lock and review workflow. Final integration reruns the small smoke scenarios from clean state and verifies teardown.

## Agent-loop execution contract

Read this epic before every child task. Work only inside this prototype subtree: select an unblocked open leaf task, inspect it, claim with your harness actor and owner ct, sync, implement in the dedicated worktree, verify, append evidence, close and sync. Parent ownership is not a child claim. Respect existing reservations. Close a feature only when its children and feature-level smoke outcomes are complete, then continue to the next feature. Do not stop just because the first demo works, and do not select unrelated ready work outside this subtree.

All prototype work is AFK-eligible: no hitl label or human assignment gates are planned. Missing product details should be resolved conservatively under this directive, with a recorded prototype decision, rather than sent back as a new grilling round. Genuine external blockers, tracker sync conflicts, unsafe process ownership, missing credentials or new destructive scope still require an honest stop/report; autonomy is not permission to force them. Do not close blocked/unverified acceptance as done or hide it with a substitute fixture.

At completion leave a reviewable prototype branch, concise user usage/demo instructions, command/API reference, architecture and schema notes sufficient to continue, and evidence for all runnable scenarios. Report library use (including actual ts-pattern and XState paths), limitations and an evidence-based assessment of ship-readiness. No automatic integration/deployment. Original epic untouched throughout.

The final native probe and clean-room documentation/smoke task can be worked independently after the operator feature, so missing credentials need not prevent local verification work; completion still requires the real native acceptance or an honestly open blocker.

comments.author: indigo-pleased-jay
comments.text:
Consultation complete: the proposed Tooling / Release-workflow split fits Hive's existing ownership. This is design advice, not final implementation approval or permission to publish a release.

Evidence: hv-e8i94.1.3.2, filed closed with evidence:architecture, linked to this stage and hv-e8i94.1.1/hv-e8i94. Local/unpublished. Return acceptance, departures and final-review outcomes to this same topic thread.

Evidence and reuse. I read hv-e8i94, hv-e8i94.1.1, the assigned run/stage and scout hv-ytvdk, then inspected root/package instructions, philosophy, architecture, glossary, Busy Bee SPEC/authoring guide, Land, package builds, install-artifacts.ts, Colony executable resolution and Hive UI's embedded-asset build. Baseline HEAD was 1528fce360b3adf4a0391168f7ac4446237e964e; the worktree was initially clean and the implementation owner began editing it during this consultation. This is a source-grounded consult, not a verdict on that evolving diff. No ADR directory exists. A closed-inclusive Homebrew architectural-evidence lookup and source-task incoming links found no prior record for this question. The release/BV intent is supplied in the coordinator-authored beads, not an independently supplied original user transcript.

1. Keep the release module in lib/tooling and the orchestration in proposed .workflows/release/{busybee.toml,workflow.ts}. Tooling should hide version/changelog preparation, clean-revision builds, archive assembly, hashing and formula rendering behind a few typed operations. A sufficient interface is prepare(explicit version, previous release identity), package(exact commit, selected supported targets, output directory) -> artifact manifest, and formula(manifest, release destination) -> Ruby text. These are semantic operations, not requirements for particular filenames or exported names. Keep Git/filesystem/subprocess effects injected into this module; compose native adapters at its CLI. The same-revision manifest is a build receipt, not a second release scheduler or authoritative task store. No new product package, Shared release framework or runtime dependency from product CLIs to Tooling is justified by this sole repository consumer.

2. Reuse each package's build contract, adding target selection there rather than copying its compiler arguments into an independent release matrix. lib/tooling/README.md:47-64 and the package scripts show the existing contracts. In particular, Busy Bee needs both --compile-autoload-package-json and --compile-autoload-tsconfig; Hive UI builds HTML/Tailwind assets through lib/hive-ui/scripts/build.ts; Colony resolves siblings via process.execPath in lib/colony/src/executables.ts:7-23. Keep all five Colony executables together, and assemble exactly the nine authorized binaries. The release artifact list is smaller than the set of manifests being versioned: Beads, Shared, Tooling and Waggle still receive the suite version; Waggle's binary is excluded. Do not package whichever dist files happen to exist or run install:bin/mise bootstrap to build an archive. Root package.json's prepare hook configures repository tooling, so detached dependency installation must explicitly account for lifecycle hooks and inherited tracker context.

3. One explicit release version should update every agreed package manifest; each distributed executable should statically import its own package version. That keeps runtime package independence and makes compiled version output describe the compiled revision. Check the runtime/worker/watchdog companions as well as the public CLIs: their baseline entrypoints do not all offer harmless --version paths. Keep .workflows/*/busybee.toml compatibility versions independent, as SPEC's saved-run rules require. Derive changelogs from a verified prior suite tag and the candidate history; label unchanged package entries clearly. If entries are path-local, do not imply that "no package-local changes" means a shared dependency had no behavioral effect. No local tags were present; I did not refresh remote history. Define the initial-release baseline explicitly rather than quietly treating an unavailable tag as an empty release.

4. Use an explicit Release chart with preparation, Land/evidence, packaging verification, external publication and tap-update stages. The worker executes release commands; XState actions/task renderers remain pure, per docs/busybee-workflows.md and lib/busybee/SPEC.md. Existing Land owns code checks/review/integration/local installation; do not copy or weaken those gates and do not add release publication to ordinary Land. The simplest initial composition is a driver-handled stage that starts and waits for the named Land run, retaining its ID and using completedTasks: [] while Release is unfinished. This does not require embedding the entire Land chart or changing Busy Bee. Carry canonicalRoot, BEADS_DB, exact integrated revision, tag, artifact receipt and evidence locations beyond feature-worktree removal. The named Release definition must be present compatibly in the surviving checkout. Snapshot receipts are evidence; they do not independently prove that a release or tap commit exists.

5. Bind the tag, archive manifest, checksums and formula to one exact integrated commit. Packaging from a clean detached checkout is a good seam: verify the requested commit/version, use frozen dependencies, and retain the compiler version/target and artifact hashes. If integration brings in changes affecting the prepared release history, reconcile the changelogs and checks before fixing that identity. Prefer building and verifying archives before pushing the release tag/public release: failed cross-builds then do not consume a public version. A local tag may precede packaging if its resolved commit is fixed. This ordering is a proposal, not a previously settled rule. For external publication, use an explicit repository and verify the remote tag's commit; gh release create --verify-tag prevents GitHub CLI from silently creating a missing tag at default-branch HEAD. After an interrupted external write, inspect actual tag/release/assets and compare them with the retained receipt before resuming; on mismatch, fail with the precise next action instead of overwriting tags/assets. GitHub's documented behavior: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_create .

6. A same-repository tap is technically supported and is the smallest deployment proposal here. Put the generated formula at Formula/hive.rb and document `brew tap codethread/hive https://github.com/codethread/hive.git`, then the fully qualified `brew install codethread/hive/hive`. The explicit URL matters: the one-argument tap form assumes homebrew-hive. Homebrew's contract is https://docs.brew.sh/Taps ; the supplied read-only example already uses the same pattern at /Users/ct/dev/projects/skein-src/README.md:235 and Formula/millstrand.rb. Reuse its location/distribution idea, not its Go/source-build implementation. Keeping Formula/hive.rb in Hive avoids creating another repository, but does not itself decide initial version, public release destination or authorize external publication. Its formula bump must be a later commit than the source release commit, because archive hashes are only known after building; do not chase a self-referential formula/hash/tag cycle or retag the suite after the bump. Keep the old valid formula until new public assets are available; the first formula cannot be truthfully usable before the first artifacts exist. Publish/verify assets, then land the formula-only update through normal repository policy. The resulting main commit can intentionally be newer than the release tag.

7. The formula installs prebuilt files into its own keg and requires both dicklesworthstone/tap/br and dicklesworthstone/tap/bv. I re-read /Users/ct/dev/dots/mise.toml:100-101 and verified the upstream Formula/br.rb and Formula/bv.rb at https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/homebrew-tap/tree/main/Formula . Do not make BV optional, invoke repo bootstrap, start a service, or reuse the local ~/.local/bin installer from the formula. Explicit platform selection and actual per-archive SHA256 values are sufficient; no source-build fallback is needed. Bun documents darwin/linux x64/arm64 cross-targets at https://bun.com/docs/bundler/executables , but successful cross-compilation does not verify execution on those platforms. State the supported matrix and actual smoke evidence separately. Acceptance evidence should include archive contents/version agreement, an install outside Hive, a real representative operation, Busy Bee external workflow loading, and Colony companion resolution without starting the user's shared daemon. Homebrew's test guidance supports functional smoke tests: https://docs.brew.sh/Formula-Cookbook#add-a-test-to-the-formula .

Trade-offs. Adapting the existing builders preserves package-specific build knowledge and prevents stale compiler flags. A small Tooling module buys locality for version/history/artifact invariants; a generic publishing framework or another shared service would add callers' knowledge without current consumers. The same-repository tap trades a larger tap checkout and a post-release formula commit for avoiding another repository, credentials surface and duplicated configuration. No new database, release scheduler or cross-package product imports are needed. Maintained-tool comparison/research is already assigned to the implementation owner; this consult does not substitute for that work or declare an unexamined release library the winner.

Unresolved decisions and verification. The owner must record the accepted destination/tap choice, first version and history baseline, supported targets and publishing authorization before performing the corresponding effects. The existing-repository tap is my recommendation, not accepted user policy. The implementation can proceed while those external values remain explicit inputs; this consult itself is not blocked by them. Next useful evidence is a final diff plus the owner's current checks, isolated install/build proofs, Release transition evidence including post-Land continuation, and actual publication receipts when authorized. No tests, builds, installs, credential checks, remote publication or implementation/document changes were performed by this consultation. All examined tasks retain their owners and state; only the assigned report workflow and linked evidence are updated.

Architectural depth should move that knowledge into lib/beads. Prior contract fixes on hv-ebh1g.9 are reported passing by the coordinator; this consultation does not reverify those repairs.

2. Concrete recommendation. Adopt the published scope-first shape: create(scope,input), show(scope,id), list(scope,selection), search(scope,text,selection), ready(scope,selection), update(scope,ids,input), close(scope,id,options), where(scope). Retain native names for groups comments.add/list, dep.add/remove, query.save/list/run/delete, sync.import/flush/merge/status. Scope is {cwd,db?,actor?}; explicit db/actor override flags and env, omission preserves native invocation/discovery, memory omission uses fixture defaults. Keep the injected factory unbound; per-call scope prevents actor/tracker leakage across Colony repositories. A mutable selected session is unnecessary. Owner and assignee remain operation data, independent of actor. Preserve native ifUnchanged, claim, force, explicit empty-string clears and limit:0.

Use native argv construction and JSON parsing only inside the live adapter; implement memory operations directly against typed records/filters. JSON fields can retain native names; named input fields can use TypeScript camelCase. Keep CommandError identity/native diagnostics for existing conflict policy. Preserve caller-owned recipe/checkpoint decoding, workflow beforeWrite timing, selection/closure policy and browser projections. These remain product responsibilities even after native record parsing moves.

Before consumers freeze on service.ts, close these concrete declaration gaps:
- Scope/read options must express noAutoImport/noAutoFlush for UI reads; bootstrap sync.status must preserve its explicit no-side-effect inspection. Do not globally suppress native auto-sync and thereby change other consumers.
- BeadRecord currently inherits id/type-only relationships from Bead. show must expose the native relation title/status/priority fields required by UI detail; callers must not extend/reparse a thin schema to recover data the adapter discarded.
- Keep distinct command result shapes. Native update returns compact nullable owner/assignee receipts; close returns compact receipts. Native create uses exported dependency objects, while show has hydrated relation details; ready is a summary without hydrated relations/design. A common required detail type must not fabricate facts or cause hidden extra show calls. Use the smallest consumed DTO per command; retaining a narrow Bead structural input for Shared decoders avoids forcing unrelated fixtures to invent full native records. list has total; search does not. Clarification to early comment6438: create does return a native exported issue; the concern is equating that with hydrated show detail, not denying its record fields.
- UpdateBead extends Partial<CreateBead> currently admits deps, which native update does not accept. Define supported update fields explicitly (or omit create-only fields); keep label replacement/addition/removal unambiguous.

UI query diagnostics need one typed read-to-argv formatter shared with the native adapter, or native read observation metadata; choose the smaller concrete solution with the UI worker. A display-only formatter accepts named read inputs and exposes no executable generic run. Preserve current query/log behavior; do not rebuild transport argument logic in UI. sync mutations may return void because existing callers ignore stdout; sync.status returns native facts while Tooling retains its healthy-workspace predicate. Memory sync fails visibly. Saved queries store typed filters, never argv.

3. Trade-offs. Named methods add declarations but remove CLI syntax, duplicate native schema knowledge and the fake parser from every consumer. Per-call scope repeats a small object but preserves independent execution, tracker and actor authority. Separate response shapes avoid inaccurate full-record promises and extra I/O. Adding only consumed flags avoids recreating all of br or adding compatibility machinery.

4. Limits/next evidence. No further user policy decision blocks this design; worker publication and focused native/memory results must settle exact consumed DTOs and UI diagnostics. Final architectural review remains required after migration. This is advice on a live draft, not acceptance of the completed implementation. comments.text:
Changes needed — architecture review hv-ebh1g.7, 2026-10-11.

Scope and governing intent
Reviewed the working candidate against 9aa6532c183c47d37b84aebdc00a78859167e8ec, including untracked lib/beads and new consumer/selection tests. The governing decision is hv-ebh1g's accepted raw BeadsCall {args,cwd,db?,actor?}/BeadsService.run -> Promise<string>, standalone @hive/beads per the user corrections in hv-lmvfo, behavior preservation, and native parity for the subset consumed by Hive. docs/architecture.md retains task-state authority in native Beads; lib/busybee/SPEC.md delegates closure policy to native Beads, including worker-created subtasks. No implementation, architecture documentation or other implementation tasks were changed.

Verified findings (all P2: incorrect memory semantics can make consumer behavior tests disagree with production)

1. Separate close policy from ready/start policy. lib/beads/src/memory.ts:330 calls blockingIssues and activeChildren, but activeChildren at :824 returns nothing for non-epic parents and blockingIssues at :668 recursively inherits ancestor blockers. Both are incorrect for close. With a task parent and an open child, native br 0.7.4 refuses close (exit 3, NOTHING_TO_DO, "parent issue has 1/1 open children"), while memory closes the parent. Conversely, with an epic blocked by a prerequisite and a child with no direct blocker, native permits closing the finished child, while memory refuses it because of its parent's prerequisite. This directly affects Busy Bee: createTask fixes issue type to task (lib/busybee/src/native.ts:193), and closeTask/:215 plus runtime.ts:727/:740 close run/grouping/worker records. Recommendation: preserve the existing readiness distinction (a task parent remains ready while an epic with open children is excluded), but give close its actual all-parent child gate and direct close-blocker semantics. Add both cases to the bounded differential relation scenario; its current epic/direct-blocker case at lib/beads/tests/contract/scenarios.ts:151 cannot distinguish these policies. Focused reproduction: bun /tmp/beads-hierarchy-probe.ts; disposable native tracker removed afterward. Both adapters returned the same ready rows, while their close outcomes disagreed in the two ways above.

2. Claim must reject deferred targets without changing them. lib/beads/src/memory.ts:265 checks assignment and closed status but omits status=deferred and a future defer_until. Native rejects either with exit 4 / VALIDATION_FAILED / field=claim and preserves the record. Memory instead assigns the actor and sets in_progress. This is observable through the real Colony consumer, not just adapter output: acquireClaim (lib/colony/src/claims.ts:10) returned conflict with native and claimed with memory for each fixture. Native updated_at was unchanged; memory changed it. This matters when deferral is present at the authoritative claim check, including a race after eligibility sampling. Recommendation: match the native claim-target guard and extend the claim contract with both status and future-date deferral, asserting refusal and unchanged state. Focused reproduction: bun /tmp/beads-claim-probe.ts; four consumer calls against disposable native and pure-memory adapters, cleanup completed.

3. List filtering must not reuse ready's deferral exclusion. lib/beads/src/memory.ts:477 drops deferred status/future defer_until unless --deferred or --include-deferred is present, even for list --all / --status all. Native list --all --limit 0 returned deferred and future-dated open records; memory omitted both. Native list --status open --limit 0 returned the future-dated open record; memory omitted it. These are consumed list shapes in Colony request discovery/listing and Busy Bee fixture queries; --all must mean native all, independently of readiness. Recommendation: implement command-specific deferral selection and add these cases to filtersAndPagination, preserving ready exclusion. Focused reproduction: bun /tmp/beads-architecture-probe.ts, with the native and memory fixture clocks on the current date and a 2099 deferral. No configurable policy engine is needed for these default native semantics.

Aligned observations
- lib/beads owns the raw command interface, native/memory adapters, consumed schema and canonical CommandError without importing Hive packages. Shared retains repository endpoints and spawn-domain meaning; lint import direction and browser restrictions match the accepted standalone package policy.

You are the Hive scout: a read-only code finder. Locate existing code and return a navigation map for a reader who will re-read the important files. Report paths, symbols and short factual labels, not architectural interpretation or proposed changes.

Repository content is read-only. Use Bash only for inspection and the required local reporting and closure of your assigned lookup tasks, plus your own Bee completion. Do not edit source, create implementation tasks, change other tasks, commit application code or delegate work.

## Scope boundary

Take the lookup instructions from the assigned task when present, otherwise from the user. Check scope before searching code:

- One concrete lookup, including its direct callers and tests: proceed.
- One lookup plus analysis: do the lookup and note that analysis is outside Scout's scope. Leave the task open if its acceptance requires that analysis; report the handoff as blocked.
- Several unrelated domains or a system-wide change assessment: do not explore. Record a reply of at most 40 words asking for one concrete lookup, leave the task open and report blocked.

Design comparisons, recommendations, correctness or concurrency reasoning, implementation plans and effort/LOC estimates belong to other bees. "Read-only" does not turn analysis into a lookup.

## Strategy

1. Use `rg` to narrow the search quickly; `fd` and `tree` can help when available. Include hidden project directories; exclude dependency/build output, not first-party code.
2. Read matching definitions and direct references. For tests, read assertions rather than relying on test names or symbol matches. Read targeted sections of large files.
3. Before writing the report, print the source evidence for the final map together: `rg -n` for exact definitions/references and numbered source for test assertions. Copy locations from this output, not memory; drop unverified details. Reporting and completion commands may follow this final evidence check.
4. Return the smallest useful set of pointers. Direct callers/importers reference the requested symbol; omit adjacent layers, internal helpers and documentation unless the lookup needs them. A symbol search alone cannot establish absent coverage: follow the caller's output fields to assertions. Say "not found in <searched scope>", not "does not exist".

## Report

Record the map on each assigned lookup task before closing it; use the same map as your response. A lookup report does not authorize closing implementation work it examines.

Return a single **Files** list ordered for re-reading, one bullet per file:

`path:verified-line` — `identifier(s)`: brief factual lookup label.

Use repository-root-relative paths and exact lines from the final evidence check. Include only identifiers needed to find the code, not signatures, copied implementations, file lengths or invented range endpoints. For tests, name the assertion topic rather than scenario details.

Aim for 100–200 words, fewer for simple lookups. Preserve every requested direct consumer even if that exceeds the budget. No preamble, duplicate lists or completion summary.

Add **Notes** only when the lookup cannot be fully answered: missing matches, search limits or analysis left out of scope. Do not add unsolicited claims about coverage, architecture or behavior.

description:
{"cwd":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/feat--workflow-task-parents","effort":"high","harness":"codex","kind":"librarian","model":"gpt-6-astra","prompt":"","system_prompt":"When launched by Colony, follow its execution runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and record the updates locally. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships. Publish only at the root runbook’s explicit remote-exchange checkpoints. Return the evidence ID and local/publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and record the updates locally. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships. Publish only at the root runbook’s explicit remote-exchange checkpoints. Return the evidence ID and local/publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.

- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Record authorized Beads updates locally and follow the existing runbook’s publication checkpoints; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.
