title: Why the task card hides completed Bee details and shows unknown activity
description:
{"formatVersion":1,"taskId":"hv-7drcd.2","requestId":"hv-q8k5l","author":"red-worthy-wolverine","body":"The reported card is showing native task assignment without an eligible current Bee-request match. The Bee metadata has not been lost. The misleading part is that the card still renders “Activity unknown” when there is no matched request.

Verified facts (2026-10-16):

- `hv-7drcd` remains `in_progress`, assigned to `amber-civic-crawdad`, as instructed until integration. Its notes explicitly identify request `hv-tipv6`; its delivery comment records commit `815d257`.
- `bee status hv-tipv6 --json` identifies a `slow-worker` Bee using Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, effort `xhigh`. The request succeeded and closed at 2026-10-14 20:10:15 UTC. Its last recorded stdout is 20:10:05 UTC. Its exact assigned work is the closed run `hv-7drcd.1`, not the parent feature `hv-7drcd`.
- Thus this request fails two independent card-attribution conditions: it is completed, and the parent feature is not in its direct requested-work membership. Keeping the external feature open does not keep the request running.

Current implementation and accepted intent:

1. `lib/hive-ui/server/data.ts:340` enriches assigned in-progress cards from the open request inventory. At `:737`, `beeAssignments` requires native `in_progress`, pending request outcome, exact assignee/identity equality and direct `request.taskIds` membership. `contracts.ts:158` documents this narrow projection. Completed history, a friendly-looking name and parent-child relationships do not satisfy it.
2. `src/ui.tsx:140` returns no assignment indicator for an empty match list. With matches, it renders a small `UserRound` icon with “Bee assigned” for accessibility; kind and request ID live in the hover title. The card projection omits harness/model/effort. Request views already carry kind/harness/model/outcome and recorded observations; the current Bee DTO does not include effort.
3. `src/bead-card.tsx:62` nevertheless renders `BeeActivity` for every assigned in-progress card, constructing `{ outcome: "pending", stdout: latest?.stdout ?? null }`. With no match this becomes pending/null; `src/activity.ts:10` returns unknown and `src/ui.tsx:20` labels it “Activity unknown”. Its tooltip even refers to a “current attempt” that has not been established. The label is absence of evidence in this projection, not a finding that `hv-tipv6` is still running or stalled.

`docs/design/hive-ui.md:150` deliberately defines the active/direct indicator. Existing evidence `hv-ux3m` records its accepted predicate and the later accepted output-recency presentation. It also records the prior choice of a subtle icon without a visible assignment pill/text. Its latest review preserves terminal outcomes as ended and defers non-Bee activity evidence. This is a presentation/expectation gap, not evidence that an agent ignored an instruction to show historical Bee identity.

The three meanings should remain separate: native assignee answers who is assigned; an exact recorded request supplies Bee kind and captured execution attributes for that request; timestamped output/observations supply historical execution evidence. A Bee is an agent running as a configured kind, not a permanent identity category. Neither friendly-name shape nor hierarchy proves that classification or present activity.

Recommended smallest direction — proposal, not accepted implementation:

- In `src/bead-card.tsx`, only render Bee activity when an actual matching pending request exists. Retain unknown for a real pending request without stdout. Keep annotation loading/failure notices separate; absence of a badge must not assert that no Bee exists.
- Keep the existing compact current-assignment projection. Make its request references inspectable through a keyboard-accessible disclosure/link in `src/ui.tsx` and the selected detail surface, preserving every matching request rather than selecting a supposedly unique identity. Show the captured kind/harness/model and outcome in request detail; add effort only if requested by that consumer.
- If historical provenance is desired, present “Recorded Bee request — completed” separately in selected detail, using exact request IDs and recorded provenance, outcome and original timestamps. Own that read model in Hive UI (`server/data.ts`, `contracts.ts`, `src/inspector.tsx`) and reuse the existing request/detail route and resource ownership. Do not broaden `beeAssignments` to completed requests or reuse historical output as a pending activity signal. No new identity registry, Colony service or polling is needed.

The unresolved product decision is whether task details should expose historical Bee participation after completion, and what explicit evidence associates an external parent task with that request. Here the association is supplied in authored task notes; it is not a direct execution membership. Do not infer it from parent links or silently parse free-form notes into authority. Adding the parent to a spawn's `related` work merely to light up the UI is also wrong: Shared interprets those edges as requested task IDs (`lib/shared/src/spawn-request.ts:380`). Historical disclosure must not change completion ownership. A visible “Bee/kind” label would also deliberately revise the earlier icon-only choice.

For this case now, inspect `hv-tipv6` directly, or locate it in Bees → Completed with appropriate history paging and closed-work filters. Its completed request details are the relevant evidence; the parent card's unknown badge is not.

Evidence and limits: current source at `b0738fc0d07eb6adc33bc8e01e2ae5c326e9db6a`, native exact-ID reads, current design/glossaries, and Honeybee response `hv-7ivd5` from succeeded request `hv-2m3pz` / completed nested run `hv-7drcd.2.2`. I read the returned response and inspected selected records `hv-ux3m`, `hv-ygcne.4.9.1.2` (read attribution versus execution authority) and `hv-7drcd.1.4.2` (selected retained logs). Honeybee's closed-inclusive bounded discovery covered all 46 labelled architecture records and focused topic matches; this consultation makes no repository-wide recurrence claim. Existing evidence thread: `hv-ux3m`; local selected tracker only, no remote synchronization.

No code/docs, original feature status/assignment, request lifecycle or implementation acceptance was changed. This is source-and-tracker consultation, not a reproduced browser screenshot or installed-build verification. No checks/tests were rerun because there is no implementation change. The proposed presentation and historical-provenance policy remain unimplemented and unvalidated.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Obtain the task bead if one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

comments.text:
Busy Bee preflight architecture and test isolation — hv-mcrp4
2026-10-11 · librarian purple-wet-badger

The architecture is adequate at the package and engine-lifecycle level. A small internal refactor is warranted for data-only policy tests and shared task rendering; a general workflow-inspection model followed by a separate pure-assessment layer is not justified by the current callers. I found concrete locality/testability debt, not a newly demonstrated functional defect or a reason to reverse hv-4nx39.7's aligned verdict.

This is advisory. The changes below are proposals, not accepted intent or implementation authorization. No application code, tests, documentation, timing registry, timeouts, commits or PR state changed.

Verified source: branch fix/workflow-recovery-guidance; HEAD 5dd50a195ef986bb9c57c241bd8f2e792ccd317c; tree 57d6ee22e8828691909294b3c57a982c8abd8a96; clean index and worktree at inspection. Scope: Busy Bee preflight, loaders, restoration, projection/rendering and relevant tests. Read hv-mcrp4, hv-4nx39, hv-e928a, final review hv-4nx39.7 and the complete known evidence hv-if4ol. The task supplies ct's concern and timing permission as coordinator-recorded conversation evidence; no original voice transcript was supplied. This is one decision thread, not a repository-wide audit or recurrence claim.

Evidence and caller map

| Responsibility | Current owner, callers and test seam | Judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest/config validation | catalogue.ts:62 namedDefinition -> readManifest:94; listWorkflows:38 shares it. Consumers: runtime.startNamed:135, runtime.loadRetainedDefinition:403, CLI schemaSource:250, preflight.candidateSource:184. Services inject Git, directory/text/file reads. | Adequate. Test schema/path/absence behavior through namedDefinition with an in-memory Services adapter. No actor, tracker or new config service is required. |
| Imported definition/input validation | definition.ts:78 load fingerprints and parses importModule output; readInput:92 parses external JSON/inputSchema; validate:104 uses initialTransition. Runtime initialization, CLI validation/input-schema and preflight are consumers of load. | Adequate. Invalid exports/input and import/hash order can use these existing interfaces with fake import/read operations. validate checks initial semantics, so a small real XState machine is appropriate. |
| Native JSON and checkpoint loading | native.ts:134 resolveEndpoint, :158 tracker, :168 readBead; checkpoint.ts:85 readCheckpoint. Runtime reads and preflight.inspectCheckpoint:203 consume the decoded Run. | Adequate. Existing unit/checkpoint.test.ts already exercises JSON/header refusal without actors. Native subprocess output and author files still need boundary parsing. |
| Version policy | compatibility.ts:14 compatibleWorkflowVersion; consumed by runtime.loadRetainedDefinition:408 and preflight.assessRun:155. | Already a useful pure seam, with unit/compatibility.test.ts covering the matrix. No engine fixture needed for another SemVer row. |
| XState interpretation | definition.ts:124 actorFor, :138 childActors, :146 declaresEvent, :161 targetActor; runtime and preflight consume them. | Adequate. Dynamic XState typing stays here. Event-descriptor tables already use declaresEvent directly in unit/events.test.ts. |
| Active task projection | runtime.ts:204 frontier, :693 nodeEntry, :716 titledAncestor. Consumers are runtime.assertOpenParents:659, publish:741 and preflight.assessFrontier:268. | Real reuse already exists. Keep the single _nodes interpretation; preflight -> runtime is acyclic and within Busy Bee. File movement alone improves no behavior. |
| Effective task rendering | runtime.entryCreation:834 and preflight.assessFrontier:279 independently invoke task, merge overrides and parse ResolvedTask. | Concrete duplication at two production consumers. A small shared render operation has a semantic purpose beyond test speed. |
| Per-run assessment | preflight.ts:137 assessRun; production caller inspectCheckpoint:235, plus direct tests and the parallel producer regression. | Already separates loading/native IO from assessment. It takes typed Run + Definition + candidate version, not Services or JSON. It still restores an actor and runs author schema/render callbacks, as its contract requires. |
| Discovery/report/CLI | preflight:94 resolves candidate, lists/filters/reads native records; inspectCheckpoint:203 retains per-run findings; cli.registerPreflight:193 adds envelope/exit semantics. | Keep orchestration here. Services is an adequate IO seam; no new injectable actor factory or general repository interface is needed. |

Important distinction: the direct assessRun tests do not initialize a Busy Bee run, acquire a lock, create Beads, import files, parse checkpoint JSON or select a tracker. They construct a never-started XState actor from a typed saved fixture. Calling all of that “full engine machinery” would misdiagnose the current code. The larger lifecycle tests do run start/submit/publication, with an in-memory native adapter; the preflight CLI tests exercise command/report wiring with fake IO. The tests/integration directory name does not establish that a test uses a live database.

Trust and restoration

The small formatVersion/locator/hash/id header in checkpoint.ts:18-25 establishes the explicitly accepted engine-body trust contract. readCheckpoint returns the engine-owned body as Run; keep that deliberate assertion and no legacy decoder, recursive body schema, shim or repair. A valid header is not proof that a candidate author's changed chart can restore that body: preflight's structural/context/command assessment answers a different question and is not redundant checkpoint validation.

Preflight currently parses descriptions for attribution before invoking readCheckpoint. The narrow diagnosticIdentitySchema at preflight.ts:27 and checkpointIdentity:402 allow unrelated and completed runs to be filtered before unsupported-format diagnostics are attributed. That is not a legacy run decoder: it never restores old bodies. The repeated JSON parse on matching records could be removed locally if measurement identified it as material, preserving the same filter order, but it does not justify a new loading architecture. Do not eliminate native or author-input validation to get below a timing threshold.

Keep real XState restoration in structural tests. Installed XState 5.33.2's StateMachine-521e1f66.esm.js:498 restores children, skips an unresolved child source, resolves active nodes and revives serialized actor references in context. raise-97446fd4.esm.js:643 catches restoration exceptions into error snapshots. Therefore actor construction success alone is insufficient, verifyActorTree at preflight.ts:348 earns its keep, and structuredClone before restoration protects the saved object. Hand-written actor/inspection fakes would bypass precisely these risks. XState's official persistence reference explains deep persistence and changed-logic compatibility caveats (https://stately.ai/docs/persistence#caveats); the installed v5 source, rather than today's documentation version, establishes the exact implementation inspected. Pure initialTransition is already used for creation validation; it is not a substitute for restoring the saved actor tree.

Minimal proposed design

1. Separate raw root-context assessment from actor-tree bookkeeping within preflight.ts.

   Proposed internal-module interface:
   assessResumeContext(rawContext: unknown, schema: Definition["resumeSchema"]): Finding

   Today assessContext:363 accepts a restored root plus the whole snapshot and Definition, but its root rule uses only the RAW persisted root context and optional schema (:373-378). The actor is needed solely for the separate child_contexts uncertainty finding at :393. Have assessRun compose these two concerns. The helper should return the root finding directly, parse a clone, compare declared output fields against raw input, leave stripped undeclared fields alone, and never return converted context for use in restoration.

   Move the missing-schema and default/transform/strip policy rows to this interface. Keep representative assessRun wiring coverage proving that the persisted root, not revived actor context or inputSchema, is supplied and that child contexts remain unchecked. Preserve the current orchestration/report behavior, including its restoration gating, unless a separately reviewed change explicitly intends additional findings on restoration failure.

   This is a legitimate domain seam: “does this candidate resume contract accept the existing root data unchanged?” It need not know a machine, native bead or whole Run. Author schemas remain trusted callbacks, so stateless engine logic does not promise to sandbox their effects.

2. Share effective task resolution at the existing definition seam.

   Proposed interface in definition.ts:
   renderTask(metadata: Metadata, context: Record<string, unknown>): ResolvedTask

   Move the common task invocation, record-result validation, metadata override merge and final resolvedTaskSchema parse out of runtime.entryCreation:834 and preflight.assessFrontier:279. Both production callers use it. Runtime still chooses entering context and owns visit allocation/publication; preflight still chooses savedVisit.context ?? currentEntry.context and passes a clone. The helper does not choose a visit, read a checkpoint, find a frontier or publish work. Preserve each caller's current context ownership; do not silently make runtime clone/migrate context as part of this extraction.

   This reduces a real risk: preflight could otherwise certify a task contract using subtly different override/validation rules than the publisher. It also makes renderer behavior testable with Metadata and context, without constructing a chart. Existing types/schemas and IO ownership stay where they are; no new package or service.

3. Narrow the existing frozen-command rule rather than building a whole assessment model.

   Make preflight.ts:335 verifyCommands a small testable internal export accepting the saved command map, proposed command map and candidate commandSchemas (or equivalently narrow typed picks), instead of whole ActiveEntry/ResolvedTask/Definition objects. Preserve the existing throw/finding adapter. Its rule is already independent of actors: every saved choice must retain its event and have a candidate schema; additional candidate choices are allowed. Use data tables for those cases. Do not infer payload compatibility from schema presence.

   Keep the one assessRun event/command wiring case and the frozen-context renderer case. Continue to use definition.declaresEvent for declaration checks, not actor.can, guard evaluation or an imitation transition engine. Do not export check/reportStatus merely so tests can inspect trivial implementation details.

These are small functions in existing modules, not a new public @hive/busybee contract. The package currently exports runtime.ts; no package export expansion or Shared/Colony change is needed.

Why not a general inspectWorkflow -> assessCompatibility pipeline?

Its proposed observation record would have to encode restoration errors, missing child logic, actor routes/nodes, context-schema outcomes, renderer errors, effective tasks and event declarations. Most of those observations already ARE the substantive compatibility findings. The subsequent “pure assessor” would largely combine statuses and compare command maps. There is one production orchestration consumer, no second independent inspector, and no established need to serialize or reuse this intermediate representation.

Such a split adds an extra contract and encourages tests built from invented inspection records while the difficult producer behavior remains in the inspector. Passing an actor-restoration callback through Services would similarly move complexity into fake adapters rather than isolate actual IO. Keep assessRun as the composition interface and extract only meaningful data rules/shared rendering. Reconsider a dedicated inspection module if a second real consumer needs the same non-starting restored view; no such caller was found in this scope.

Test allocation

| Existing behavior/case | Recommended scope |
| --- | --- |
| SemVer acceptance/rejection and required full-version syntax | Keep unit/compatibility.test.ts through existing compatibility interfaces. |
| Malformed JSON, missing/future engine format, typed payload retention | Keep unit/checkpoint.test.ts. Do not add nested-body rejection cases contrary to the trust decision. |
| Manifest name/path/schema errors; input and exported-definition validation | Exercise namedDefinition/load/readInput/validate directly with Services overrides. The older catalogue.test.ts:68 and validation.test.ts:55 tables currently use filesystem/CLI setup that most validation rows do not need. This is a separate candidate cleanup, not a reason to expand this PR silently. Retain real module-resolution/independent-dependency coverage at validation.test.ts:88 and a native catalogue path/import contract check. |
| Exact/wildcard/ancestor event declarations | Keep unit/events.test.ts using real small state nodes; these already avoid actor restoration and guards. |
| Missing resumeSchema; default/transform/strip context policy at preflight.test.ts:118,287 | Move policy rows to assessResumeContext; retain one assessment wiring case for root-only/raw-context/unknown candidate version reporting. |
| Changed frozen mapping, missing schema at :224, additional candidate choice at :311 | Put the data comparison matrix through narrowed verifyCommands. Retain the frozen visit context selection/renderer-override composition case at :311; those are not only a mapping comparison. |
| Removed root state :138; silently dropped child :154; restored child work/removed :365 | Keep real XState assessRun integration. They test dependency restoration semantics, not simple field comparison. |
| Independent findings after version/context/path/command failures :173; renderer exception and unchecked downstream command finding :202 | Keep focused assessRun composition coverage. Isolating each rule alone cannot prove continuation and report aggregation. |
| Frozen event declaration failure :337 | Keep one assessRun route-to-finding test, alongside the direct descriptor table. |
| Combined failing CLI report :34 | Retain as ct approved at measured 7–8 ms: filtering, failed/unchecked rows, standard failure envelope and exit status are its principal value. The no-write/no-start assertions remain useful but do not alone justify its whole setup. |
| Explicit --source routing :97 | Retain the small CLI wiring case with an empty tracker, as already refined; it proves option resolution/catalogue independence, not per-run restoration. It still needs its own timing decision if over budget. |
| Unsupported matching checkpoint filtering :246; malformed identity/relation/retained lock reporting :270 | Keep service-backed preflight discovery tests. They test ordering and native attribution across records; pure version or command tests do not replace them. Avoid another CLI round trip for those cases. |
| Compatible insertion at prepare and review, compatibility.test.ts:102 | Keep both startNamed -> submit -> persisted checkpoint lifecycles with startTracker. They prove distinct saved positions: visit newly inserted future work versus skip already-passed insertion, plus latest-producer persistence/downgrade refusal. Do not replace with manually prepared Run fixtures. |
| Surviving parallel visit, compatibility.test.ts:178 | Keep the complete producer -> persistence -> assessment regression. The prior actual defect overwrote the surviving context during publication. A handcrafted frozen visit would make a test pass while that defect remained. |
| Recovery collect refusal, start.test.ts:137 | Keep the mutation/lock-release/no-publication route. No actor is restored after version refusal, but the ownership lifecycle is what this test proves. Keep current paired show/discover route coverage instead of recreating the removed Cartesian matrix. |

Timing, verification and next decision

I inspected /tmp/hv-refined-test-timings.json (29 cases, three supplied fresh-process samples each). Examples: direct event cases max 0.491 ms; context default/transform/strip max 3.346/3.507/3.397 ms; missing command schema max 2.280 ms; missing child restoration max 2.985 ms; parallel lifecycle max 7.026 ms; combined report median 7.156/max 7.592 ms. Those show which tests still cross unnecessary seams; they do not establish the cost of a hypothetical refactor or prove an architectural defect by duration alone.

Also inspected the supplied refined focused log (36 pass, 0 fail, 179 assertions) and full-check log (format/lint/typechecks, 770 pass, 0 fail, 2813 assertions, 81 files). The locked execution/exit provenance is the coordinator's evidence on hv-4nx39. I ran no suites, benchmarks or source instrumentation in this advisory execution. No new performance guarantee, full standards approval or landing approval follows from this report.

Recommend the bounded extraction above before deciding allowances for the data-only context/command tests, then measure those focused cases cold again with schemas compiled at module scope. Retained XState/CLI/lifecycle cases have independent justification and should receive explicit measured-cost decisions; a larger refactor is not a prerequisite to discussing them. No warmup, test fragmentation, timeout increase or blanket 1-second band is warranted by this advice. Ct's present permission applies only to retaining the named combined reporting test around its measured 7–8 ms, not an exact registry edit or other slow cases.

The remaining user decision is whether to authorize these small refactors and the eventual per-test allowances; this advisory task does not authorize either. No unresolved domain policy blocks the investigation. Next useful evidence is the implementation owner's accepted/departed design, unchanged report/lifecycle behavior, and fresh per-case timings after any authorized extraction. Return that outcome to hv-if4ol. Existing hv-4nx39/hv-e928a remain in_review and unchanged.

Evidence capture complete: appended this consultation's compact outcome to existing closed evidence hv-if4ol, topic named-workflow-recovery-authorization / follow-up preflight-test-isolation, with a directed relates-to link to hv-mcrp4. Verified the stored entry, closed status, evidence:architecture label, retained prior advice and relationship. Delivery and evidence stay local; no remote publication checkpoint applies.

{"cwd":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive","effort":"medium","harness":"pi","kind":"scout","model":"openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol","prompt":"","system_prompt":"When launched by Colony, follow its execution runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion. In a direct user conversation, report to the user without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`; retain the supplied actor.

You are the Hive scout: a read-only code finder. Locate existing code and return a navigation map for a reader who will re-read the important files. Report paths, symbols and short factual labels, not architectural interpretation or proposed changes.

Repository content is read-only. Use Bash only for inspection and the required reporting, closure and synchronization of your assigned lookup tasks, plus your own Bee completion. Do not edit source, create implementation tasks, change other tasks, commit application code or delegate work.

## Scope boundary

Take the lookup instructions from the assigned task when present, otherwise from the user. Check scope before searching code:

- One concrete lookup, including its direct callers and tests: proceed.
- One lookup plus analysis: do the lookup and note that analysis is outside Scout's scope. Leave the task open if its acceptance requires that analysis; report the handoff as blocked.
- Several unrelated domains or a system-wide change assessment: do not explore. Record a reply of at most 40 words asking for one concrete lookup, leave the task open and report blocked.

Design comparisons, recommendations, correctness or concurrency reasoning, implementation plans and effort/LOC estimates belong to other bees. "Read-only" does not turn analysis into a lookup.

## Strategy

1. Use `rg` to narrow the search quickly; `fd` and `tree` can help when available. Include hidden project directories; exclude dependency/build output, not first-party code.
2. Read matching definitions and direct references. For tests, read assertions rather than relying on test names or symbol matches. Read targeted sections of large files.
3. Before writing the report, print the source evidence for the final map together: `rg -n` for exact definitions/references and numbered source for test assertions. Copy locations from this output, not memory; drop unverified details. Reporting and completion commands may follow this final evidence check.
4. Return the smallest useful set of pointers. Direct callers/importers reference the requested symbol; omit adjacent layers, internal helpers and documentation unless the lookup needs them. A symbol search alone cannot establish absent coverage: follow the caller's output fields to assertions. Say "not found in <searched scope>", not "does not exist".

## Report

Record the map on each assigned lookup task before closing it; use the same map as your response. A lookup report does not authorize closing implementation work it examines.

Return a single **Files** list ordered for re-reading, one bullet per file:

`path:verified-line` — `identifier(s)`: brief factual lookup label.

Use repository-root-relative paths and exact lines from the final evidence check. Include only identifiers needed to find the code, not signatures, copied implementations, file lengths or invented range endpoints. For tests, name the assertion topic rather than scenario details.

Aim for 100–200 words, fewer for simple lookups. Preserve every requested direct consumer even if that exceeds the budget. No preamble, duplicate lists or completion summary.

Add **Notes** only when the lookup cannot be fully answered: missing matches, search limits or analysis left out of scope. Do not add unsolicited claims about coverage, architecture or behavior.

You are the Hive reviewer. Check code style, test quality and documentation standards against this repository's own standards, not general taste. Architectural judgment (domain meaning, ownership, dependency direction, DI and module depth) belongs to librarian; route those questions there rather than duplicating its review.

## Standards to read first

- `AGENTS.md` and the `AGENTS.md` of every package in the change.
- `.agents/skills/typescript/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing TypeScript code.
- `.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing tests or testability changes.
- `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing repository documentation, including skills and agent instructions.

## What to inspect

- The change under review: `git diff`, `git diff --staged`, `git show <rev>`, or the files you are given.
- The surrounding code and package the change interacts with, so findings are about the actual system, not the diff in isolation.

## Checklist

- Apply the relevant skills within this review's scope; cite their rules rather than maintaining a separate checklist of their conventions here.
- Where the root architectural-review trigger applies, confirm librarian review evidence covers the final change; report missing evidence instead of substituting your own architectural verdict.

## Report format

- **Verdict** — aligned, or not aligned.
- **Findings** — ordered by severity; each one gives `path:line`, the standard it violates (file/section), and a concrete fix.
- **Confirmed** — briefly, what is aligned.
- **Not verified** — anything you could not check, and why.

## Constraints

- Never fix code: report findings only.
- Every finding cites the exact standard; without one, label it a suggestion, not a violation.
- Leave check execution and test-run evidence to the calling workflow. Assess test quality from source.

Read-only SQLite queries and current source-schema probes reproduce assignment/undefined on the first request hv-3m4 and first receipt b4cb0613-0e53-4866-a87f-1c8a9e5ff953. Operation 936140 at 2026-10-13T21:02:21.727Z failed at requests.reconcile with no completed effects. store.ts:259-265 parses all request snapshots before request.ts:251-255 filters terminal/unbound rows. Separately, readiness/status calls store.attempts -> inventory -> launchReceiptSchema (store.ts:116,205; server.ts:117), so historical receipts also break the status probe used by colony wake. A finished assessment also fails receipt.assignment; deleting/filtering only requests is insufficient.

A second, native blocker will survive resetting private state: the open request hv-wm5c7 belongs to PB-G2WYC4HJDQ.local and lacks assignment. readSpawnRequestSummary reproduces the same error before dispatch.ts:94-95 can exclude that foreign host. Current local request hv-f68p7 has a valid driver assignment for hv-itrsp and is executing through the supplied separate one-off state. Do not submit or launch another copy of it.

Recommendation (proposal, not performed)
1. Correct host admission in the existing Shared spawn representation and Colony automatic consumers. Use a small provenance projection, such as readSpawnRequestHost(bead), that parses the description's host without requiring workflow assignment. Exclude foreign and unbound records before full request hydration in automatic dispatch and closed-label recovery. Keep malformed provenance loud and keep strict driver/stage parsing, exact related anchor and private/native/receipt comparisons for every eligible local request. This is an ownership-routing seam, not legacy execution support; no default task role or nullable assignment in execution types.
2. For this entirely pre-upgrade private generation, prefer an explicit non-destructive SQLite archive operation over permanent old-format runtime support. Archiving the whole private generation avoids fixing several eager execution decoders with old-shape adapters and keeps strict execution authority intact. Archiving requests alone still leaves attempts and assessments broken; moving the whole state directory would break retained absolute artifact paths. A fresh private DB alone still encounters the foreign native request. Broad safeParse-and-skip, fabricated assignments, blanket closure/relabeling, or quota changes are inappropriate.

title: Qlock ready-ticket expiry: consultation and scoped recommendation
description:
{"formatVersion":1,"taskId":"hv-lefu1.1","requestId":"hv-in5o6","author":"maroon-active-sloth","body":"The ticket-747 incident is primarily agent invocation/resumption friction exposed by qlock's deliberate queue policy. The observed sequence is consistent with the current contract; it does not establish failed mutual exclusion. A scoped guidance follow-up is warranted. No implementation or queue-policy change is recommended on this evidence alone.

The evidence window is 301 snapshots over 06:37:24–06:47:24 BST on 16 October 2026. I inspected the supplied `cpu-qlock-evidence.json` queue changes and selected raw process/queue snapshots. The caller's reported 60-second wait timeout, later “ticket gone” diagnostic and rejoin complete the sequence; the timeout-evidence file also contains help/example matches, so raw hit counts are not counts of real failures. This is one observed resumption incident, not evidence of a recurring rate or a timing guarantee across harnesses.

- Ticket 747 was queued behind 746. Its bounded qlock invocation exited before admission. By 06:37:54 the snapshots showed 746 gone, 747 still queued and no live qlock process.
- The next observed ready reservation was `readyAt=1792129085116`, or 06:38:05.116 BST. The snapshot at 06:38:06 showed only ticket 748's waiting process, with 747 ready ahead of it. Queue advancement is demand-driven; finishing a child removes its ticket but does not itself promote the next ticket.
- The reservation expired at 06:38:35.116. Ticket 748's persisted `startedAt=1792129115173` is 06:38:35.173, 30.057 seconds after 747 became ready; the observer saw it running at approximately 06:38:36. Ticket 750 later represents the caller's deliberate rejoin. The abandoned ready reservation cost the next waiter about 30 seconds, and 747 lost its place.

Current intent is explicit in `lib/qlock/README.md:39–57,104–108`, `lib/qlock/src/run.ts:120–243` and `lib/qlock/src/queue.ts:140–166`: the wait deadline bounds admission, timeout retains the queued ticket, only a resumed/live `exec` can start its command, and a ready ticket expires after 30 seconds. Queued and ready tickets have no waiting PID or stored executable; only running tickets record qlock's PID and command. The implementation therefore cannot distinguish an absent caller from one about to resume. `status` invokes the same queue refresh: it creates no ticket and admits no child, but it can promote/expire reservations. That is documented by “Each invocation advances the queue”; it is not passive telemetry.

The recorded full-suite/check process trees were serialised. Focused tests may run outside the CPU lock under repository policy. The supplied observation did not establish a new five-second Bun timeout or concurrent full-suite holders, and the reported DANGER timing-gate failure had zero assertion failures. That separate timing failure and Colony supervisor CPU work do not establish a qlock defect. A single lock serialises participating protected commands; it is not a cap on all machine CPU activity.

My proposal is to update `lib/qlock/skills/command-queues/SKILL.md` and the execute/resume section of `lib/qlock/README.md`. The skill currently says “Use a bounded queue wait”; the README discourages `-w -1` for agents. Those instructions omit the useful distinction between a qlock admission timeout and a harness returning control while its process remains alive. This is incomplete interaction guidance, not evidence that the caller ignored an adequate asynchronous recipe.

For harnesses with a retained process session, recommend one long-lived foreground qlock invocation, using the already-supported `-w -1`, while yielding/polling the tool session briefly so the agent can communicate. For example, the command is `qlock exec --lock /tmp/agent-cpu.lock -w -1 -- bun run check`; the harness launches it with a short return/yield interval and retains its session handle. The qlock process keeps polling and claims its own turn without another model turn. Subsequent polls observe that same session; they do not enqueue another invocation. Tool-level asynchronous execution must keep the qlock process and its immediate protected child together. Shell-detaching the protected child is outside the contract.

Bounded waits remain useful when the caller deliberately needs an admission deadline or has no persistent process session. Resume the same ticket, resolved queue and intended command promptly after a real qlock timeout, and deliberately rejoin only after exit 3. A longer finite `-w` reduces exposure but cannot guarantee timely model resumption. Polling `status` after abandoning `exec` does not solve the missing execution client.

This guidance belongs with qlock's public invocation contract. A harness-specific session recipe can show its tool handles; no new contract in Shared or Colony scheduler behavior is needed. Preserve `reserveTurn`'s atomic refresh/claim transaction, the queue's single ready/running head, running-PID checks and release only after the immediate foreground child exits. `lib/qlock/src/live.ts:38–69,101–125` owns the native storage/process seam. No daemon, detached job storage or weakened ownership check is needed for this consumer.

The trade-off is retaining a lightweight waiting process and session handle. The agent must collect its exit and manage cancellation deliberately; arbitrary harness termination or process suspension still is not covered by a durable execution guarantee. Increasing the 30-second ready window would give absent callers more time but delay live followers longer; shortening it worsens the lost-place problem. A lease/heartbeat, cancellation API or persistent job service would add state and policy that this single incident does not justify. A passive status interface is a separate possible consumer need; clarify current status semantics first.

A proposed follow-up should be accepted when: (1) the two qlock guides consistently distinguish process lifetime, tool polling, admission deadline and child runtime; (2) an actual retained-session exercise under contention shows the same qlock process acquiring and running exactly once even when the agent does not revisit it within 30 seconds of availability, while the agent remains responsive; (3) the bounded-timeout path retains the same ticket, expired resumption returns exit 3, and documentation explains deliberate rejoin; (4) existing admission, FIFO/urgent non-preemption, foreground-child completion and signal ownership behavior remains intact; and (5) inspection guidance explicitly describes status as advancing state. Bookworm should own authorized repository prose changes; a CLI-help clarification, if needed, belongs in `lib/qlock/src/cli.ts` and needs explicit scope.

The user decision is whether to authorize this documentation-and-validation follow-up. A stronger requirement to preserve queue position through arbitrary agent absence would need a separate product decision about fairness and abandoned tickets. Both remain proposals. This consultation creates no implementation task and edits no repository files. Validation here was source/trace inspection; I did not run tests or a full quality suite, and the proposed retained-session scenario remains untested.

Historical discovery was delegated beneath this run to honeybee request hv-2l78m, report workflow hv-lefu1.1.2; I read its complete authored response hv-cx67o and independently inspected hv-zab4 and hv-7qrb. The latter records the supplied user approval of exec/status and explicitly explains that retained tickets still have 30-second readiness expiry. The existing archive hv-zab4 covers cumulative migration alignment, a different question. The bounded closed-inclusive lookup found no dedicated delayed-resumption thread; it is not proof that no differently worded history exists.

Architectural evidence is filed and verified as **hv-lefu1.1.3**, topic `qlock-ready-expiry-agent-resumption`, linked to the source task, consultation stage and governing history. It is a closed archive: closure means recorded, not accepted or validated. Both evidence and this response are local tracker records; no tracker synchronization, commits or application publication were performed. The report completes consultation scope only.

1. **P1 — [lib/beeswax/src/tracker-hooks.ts:100](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/feat--beeswax/lib/beeswax/src/tracker-hooks.ts:100): Husky bootstrap can make missing application policy appear successful.** The accepted run contract and librarian evidence `hv-uvd5u.5.1` comment 12324 require preserving explicit tracker application delegates, including commit-message policy, and stopping for migration when required policy is absent. `installHuskyRuntime` creates `.husky/_/<event>` wrappers before line 109 checks the configured delegate; the runner exits successfully when `.husky/<event>` is absent. A disposable native tracker accepted this configuration and its generated `commit-msg` exited 0 without the policy file. Preflight the actual application hook bodies before generating wrappers or activating the tracker runtime; report missing policy through the migration path.

The explicit-delegate path does not call `bindCheckout(root, executable, io)`; that call exists only in the no-`config.tracker` branch at line 60. With a current tracker hook section, sync from another checkout succeeded, but the tracker’s pre-commit hook failed because its own `git-path beeswax/cli` was missing. Bind the tracker checkout on the explicit-delegate path and cover both current-section and pre-integration tracker cases.

3. **P2 — [lib/beeswax/src/tracker-hooks.ts:31](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/feat--beeswax/lib/beeswax/src/tracker-hooks.ts:31): Sync can install the tracker-only runtime on an ordinary checkout.** The accepted run contract limits this shared hook exception to the permanent tracker. A same-repository database on `main` caused successful sync to set `core.hooksPath` to the tracker runtime. Validate tracker identity, including branch `tracker/state`, at the integration seam before changing worktree configuration; reject other endpoints with a migration diagnostic.

4. **P2 — [lib/beeswax/src/synchronize.ts:39](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/feat--beeswax/lib/beeswax/src/synchronize.ts:39): Update and lock refresh can erase unsupported lock identities.** The accepted project contract requires unsupported metadata to stop for user-guided migration. `update` skips `requireProjectVersion`, which also checks supported skill and owned-section identities; `commands.ts:238` similarly refreshes a release pin after checking only config equality. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and publish the updates. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish. Return the evidence ID and publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

title: Fix Honeycomb tree baseline and free pool layout
description: User observed a staircase of stale wk-pool HEADs above develop in deals-light-ui. Current tree chooses nearest strict ancestor among all registered HEADs, confusing commit history with feature stacks. Implement default-branch-relative view (discover repository default, never hardcode develop), separate flat free-pool section with ahead/behind, and infer stacks only beyond default baseline. Read-only local history, fail transparently, preserve additive JSON contract. comments.author: emerald-efficient-platypus
comments.text:
Architectural consultation for hv-n0dvx — 2026-10-13

Evidence: hv-wuo22 (closed architectural archive, saved locally; not remotely published). Delivery scope hv-g7z0r in .worktrees/fix--honeycomb-tree-baseline, actor emerald-efficient-platypus.

Recommendation: discover the default branch name from local origin/HEAD metadata, compare against a snapshotted default tip, and keep baseline presentation separate from proven feature ancestry. The user-approved correction is default-relative layout and flat free slots; local-tip preference and missing-metadata behavior below remain proposals, not established repository policy.

Evidence and reuse

Examined revision 0002d2b5f5b67c03542ad0d379a0188568558528. application/repository.ts:24 snapshots registered HEADs and compares every pair. domain/worktree.ts:249 selects nearest strict ancestors. README.md:140-150 and integration/tree.test.ts explicitly allow old branches above canonical main. hv-vj59 describes this original accepted design and records landing at 548603a. Thus the reported staircase is a limitation of the former meaning, not evidence that its implementation ignored the former guidance. No linked architectural evidence was found on hv-n0dvx or hv-vj59; closed-inclusive topic searches found no existing record for this correction.

GLOSSARY.md distinguishes default branch from canonical worktree. application/branches.ts already separates readLocalDefaultBranch (local origin/HEAD metadata), detectOriginDefaultBranch (may contact origin), and resolveOfflineDefaultBase (cached-origin-first creation policy). Reuse local discovery and GitRunner; do not use the network-capable detector or change the creation resolver's preference. PoolSlotIdentity.placeholder already identifies free slots without configuration. describeSlotRisk is unsuitable reuse: it compares a moving upstream/HEAD and substitutes zero counts on missing data.

Narrow implementation proposal

1. Resolve refs/remotes/origin/HEAD to its branch name, retaining the existing origin convention. Prefer refs/heads/<default> if present; otherwise use refs/remotes/origin/<default>. Resolve the chosen commit once and expose branch, full ref and OID as baseline metadata. The local preference serves a worktree view; cached preference serves branch creation. Neither implies the remote is current. Never guess main/develop, use canonical HEAD as default identity, read Honeycomb config, fetch, or repair metadata. Missing designation or both tips should produce an actionable typed error. A present but unreadable ref/object must fail, not trigger another fallback. Apply --no-lazy-fetch to every object-reading query, including resolution and counts.

2. Let D be baseline and H each distinct observed nonzero HEAD. Compute rev-list --left-right --count D...H: left is behind, right ahead. Establish whether a common ancestor exists in locally available history; count differences alone cannot establish that. Missing HEAD has unavailable comparison, never invented 0/0. Git execution errors remain failures; negative ancestry answers are data. No observed common ancestor is not proof of globally unrelated history in a shallow repository.

3. A feature parent P is eligible only if its group contains a non-free worktree, P shares locally observed ancestry with D, P is not reachable from D, and P is a strict ancestor of child C. Reduce eligible candidates to nearest ones with the existing domain algorithm; retain ambiguity when several remain. Do NOT require D to be an ancestor of P: that loses real stacks based on older default commits. For A--B--D with P forked at A and Q at B, P and Q remain baseline siblings; a child of P still nests beneath P after default advances. H equal to or reachable from D stays at baseline level and cannot parent features. Label reachability precisely; squash/cherry-pick integration is not established by ancestry or these counts. Do not reuse deletion-safety content-equivalence logic for this read-only view.

4. Free means worktree.pool?.placeholder, not branch-name substring and not every pooled worktree. Remove free members from feature-parent eligibility and render each slot flat with its baseline counts, including nonzero ahead. Apply this to members, not whole OIDs: an occupied worktree can share a free slot's HEAD and must retain its own stack eligibility. Group equal active HEADs without inventing parentage. Keep unrelated/no-observed-common-ancestor and missing-HEAD entries visibly separate; the minimal proposal does not infer feature stacks within unrelated history.

5. Keep orchestration and Git observations in application/repository.ts, a small tree-specific baseline resolver alongside branch discovery, pure eligibility/grouping in domain/worktree.ts, and rendering/JSON in protocol-payloads.ts. An internal readWorktreeTree(git,cwd) -> {baseline,nodes} is sufficient; no new service abstraction, registry, shared-package module or configurable baseline strategy is needed.

6. Keep kind:tree, basis:git_ancestry, flat nodes, stable OID/path IDs and existing list worktree fields. Add baseline metadata, comparison data and explicit layout/grouping metadata separate from parentage. Reserve parentage.kind=inferred for a proven strict ancestor; a header grouping old-base divergent or already-contained branches is not such an edge. Tighten parent eligibility for the new view explicitly in documentation. Keep every registered worktree represented in nodes, including free slots, and avoid synthetic worktrees or duplicate node IDs. The text renderer can project free members separately; a JSON free-pool section, if useful, should reference paths rather than create a competing inventory. Equal-HEAD identity and free-slot placement are different facts.

Trade-offs and unresolved decisions

Local-first is a defensible narrow recommendation, not yet explicit user intent; cached-first would instead show integration against last observed origin. Missing baseline metadata currently does not prevent tree output (bare/unborn tests succeed); failing changes that contract. Coordinator should explicitly record acceptance of local-first and fail-without-baseline in hv-n0dvx design, or return a user requirement for inventory-only output. Do not silently introduce a fallback mode or default override flag. A repository without origin/HEAD or using only another remote cannot satisfy this proposal without a separately decided designation source. Exact additive field names and flat labels are implementation choices; truthful distinction between grouping, equality and ancestry is required by the requested semantics.

Verification and next evidence

Consultation only: inspected source, original task history, current docs and real-Git test scenarios; no code/docs edits and no quality suites run. Confirmed Git command meanings against official documentation: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-list , https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base , https://git-scm.com/docs/git-symbolic-ref . Required implementation evidence: non-main default with canonical on another branch; local versus cached tips and absent local ref; old-base siblings and stack after default advances; contained heads; mixed free/active equal HEAD; merge ambiguity; missing metadata versus no HEAD; shallow/no-common-ancestor handling; injected Git errors and no-network/config-free behavior; JSON inventory completeness and count orientation. Return the accepted choices, final diff and outcomes to this evidence thread for architectural review. Implementation and its acceptance remain with hv-n0dvx.

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.

## Standards to read first

- `AGENTS.md` and the `AGENTS.md` of every package in the change.
- `.agents/skills/typescript/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing TypeScript code.
- `.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing tests or testability changes.

## What to inspect

- The change under review: `git diff`, `git diff --staged`, `git show <rev>`, or the files you are given.
- The surrounding code and package the change interacts with, so findings are about the actual system, not the diff in isolation.

- Apply the relevant skills within this review's scope; cite their rules rather than maintaining a separate checklist of their conventions here.
- Gates: `bun run check` passes, and test evidence covers the change's scope.
