comments.text:
Historical storage report — 2026-10-10

The recorded boundary is by responsibility and process lifetime: Colony owns durable orchestration/recovery checkpoints in private SQLite; detached supervisors and bees exchange per-execution artifacts through files. Native Beads separately owns task assignments/acceptance and spawn requests. Post-run assessments extended this existing boundary rather than introducing a second task tracker.

Historical evidence (references below are bead descriptions/design/notes, not numbered comments):
• 2026-10-04, hv-e8i.3.1 description: “Use SQLite for registry and the minimal execution bookkeeping needed, not a new persistence framework.” Its design records reservation before spawning and says “supervisor writes only owned receipts/logs.” Completion notes identify 4c2a4d5 and native smoke proving detached survival and separate tracker/cwd routing.
• 2026-10-04, hv-e8i.3.2 design/notes: durable registration and awake/asleep intent persist; temporary membership stays in server memory; remove retains attempts for later recovery; canonical policy reloads. Completed as c3c09af. This explains what needs daemon persistence rather than merely a run directory.
• 2026-10-04, hv-e8i.5.1 design: “Use artifact-only detached supervisor, persistent PID/start/command lineage, fail on ambiguous ownership.” SQLite stores XState request/attempt/claim checkpoints; immutable attempt history is retained. Notes cite 882d02f and native retry/claim evidence.
• 2026-10-04, hv-e8i.5.2 description requires executions to survive daemon exit and be adopted without duplicate launch. Notes cite 2552a99: “Durable token/fingerprint supervisor handoff records identity before launch permission.” A separate daemon-lock.sqlite is a lifetime sole-writer lock, not the task database or report store; the recorded EXCLUSIVE-to-IMMEDIATE correction came from native contention probes.
• 2026-10-04, hv-45f.1 approved design and completion notes explicitly preserve daemon/IPC, detached worker lifetimes, behavior and state locations while moving Ghost into Colony. hv-45f.11 records landing 18c6fb1 with runtime modules byte-identical apart from naming/entry plumbing. Consolidation therefore inherited the storage split; it did not originate a new storage decision. hv-45f.20 records c023363 lifecycle/diagnostics integration, not a new SQLite-versus-file rationale.
• 2026-10-08, hv-x4fu discussion notes recommend private compact assessments with artifact/source locations and offline retrieval: “creating a Beads task/report for every inspection would add unnecessary tracker lifecycle.” They require atomic terminal enrollment or idempotent derivation so a crash cannot lose/duplicate inspection, and no coupling to target outcomes/retries. This was librarian advice, subsequently adopted in hv-262w design.
• 2026-10-08, hv-262w.2 description/design specifies durable enrollment with terminal settlement, immutable private source snapshots surviving task-directory removal, SELECT-only retrieval, one launch/no automatic retry, no assessment task/spawn beads or recursion. hv-262w.5 review notes verify settlement and enrollment commit together, auxiliary receipts contain no task links, and raw transcripts do not enter Beads/list output. hv-262w.7 verifies optional task-read failures become explicit unavailable coverage committed with settlement; private persistence/ownership failures remain loud. Parent hv-262w records landing c15e7fa.
• 2026-10-09, hv-uupm design/notes retain stored schemas and SELECT-only reader unchanged. The change was presentation: selected report by default, supporting source through --request ID --source. Landed 908ac2a. It did not relocate assessment persistence.

What is stored, and where (current source verification):
Colony's colony.sqlite holds repository registration/intent; attempt launch snapshots, directory/token/state; request recovery snapshots; policy revisions; inactivity review checkpoints; and assessment snapshots. These are structured JSON snapshots inside indexed SQLite tables, not a promise that every datum is normalized. store.ts:51-61 and 115-180 show the schema and transactional terminal-request/assessment commit.

Files hold receipt.json (captured invocation/context), supervisor/process handoff and permission artifacts, atomically replaced worker.json, stdout.log/stderr.log/supervisor.log, finish.json, and auxiliary review submission/context files. docs/architecture.md explicitly says the supervisor does not reconcile Beads or write the daemon database. Colony later reads and validates these artifacts and checkpoints the observed result. A checkpoint or prepared receipt alone does not prove launch or current process liveness.

For assessments specifically, the SQLite snapshot already includes the bounded source capture and lifecycle, then receipt and accepted result. postrun.ts:373-385 writes receipt.json, source.json (captured source plus measured usage), and assessment.json (inspector context/deadline). bee assess validates recorded SQLite authority read-only and atomically submits assessment-report.json; reconciliation validates that file and stores the completed report in the assessment result (postrun.ts:250-281, 451-481). assessments.ts:44-106 reads SQLite snapshots read-only; --source additionally reads source.json. Report retrieval therefore uses the accepted/checkpointed result, not a fresh reinterpretation of the submission file.

Deliberate overlap/handoff:
The launch receipt exists in the attempt SQLite snapshot and receipt.json; the latter is the detached worker's input. Process observations live in files and are incorporated into daemon checkpoints. The assessment's bounded source exists in its SQLite snapshot and source.json; the file adds usage evidence at launch and supplies the inspector. The submitted assessment report survives as a file and is copied into the validated SQLite result. These are execution handoffs and retained evidence, not interchangeable authorities. Raw logs remain file-only; native Beads observations are minimal and can become stale.

Facts versus inference/uncertainty:
The records explicitly establish ownership, detached lifetime/recovery, reservation/handoff ordering, atomic once-only enrollment, private diagnostics and avoiding per-inspection Beads lifecycle. It follows from those facts that files let a detached supervisor communicate while Colony is absent, while SQLite coordinates durable cross-run state. That explanatory connection is an inference consistent with the documented contract. I found no standalone historical decision comparing all-file versus all-SQLite storage, no recorded performance benchmark for this split, and no explicit argument for retaining every duplicate payload after handoff. Do not attribute those rationales to ct or claim duplication was separately debated.

Verification and coverage:
Read all supplied starting records: hv-262w, hv-x4fu, hv-262w.1/.2/.5/.7, hv-uupm, hv-45f.1/.11/.20; followed only relevant prototype persistence ancestry hv-e8i.3.1/.3.2/.5/.5.1/.5.2; checked current architecture, glossary, store, launch/worker, postrun and assessment reader. Comments lists for hv-262w.5/.7, hv-uupm and hv-45f.1 were empty; their historical deliveries are in notes. A scoped SQLite search excluded system and included closed records; its first 50 results had hidden_closed_count=0 and has_more=true. This is a targeted lineage report, not an exhaustive tracker audit; unrelated results and remaining pages were not explored. No raw transcripts, live state mutation, code/config/docs edits, examined-bead changes, tests, synchronization, commits or publication. Only this assigned report task is updated; no implementation changed, so test/check suites are inapplicable.

- **architectural-friction** — 2026-10-12; topic `hive-ui-complete-family-read`; hv-28dld.1 asks how to remove the approved adaptive board's 9.7–13s cold hierarchy hydration without silently pruning native families. Areas: lib/beads and lib/hive-ui.
- **Interpretation** — Complete family membership is distinct from filtered/page-local board membership. The POC recursively hydrates full show records and awaits hierarchy inside board/detail. A smaller native read contract helps avoid comments/relationship hydration, but dep.list is one subprocess per node; replacing showMany alone is not a demonstrated optimization. Librarian proposes independent route-owned hierarchy resources, complete-summary traversal on demand, and endpoint-scoped coalesced TTL snapshots. No tracker-wide upfront graph, direct database reads, JSONL authority, second client cache, or automatic polling.
- **Resolution** — Settled user intent is preserved in hv-28dld and the accepted hv-7wcbi.5 handoff: native parent-child only; complete represented ordinary families including closed descendants; adaptive grouping independent of filtered cards; selected detail and branch navigation. The following remains librarian advice, not accepted policy: add native-shaped dep.list(scope,id,{direction,type}) to @hive/beads; keep traversal, batching, caching, HTTP schema and presentation in Hive UI; load board/detail promptly and hierarchy separately. Coalesce overlapping reads using the existing inventory startedAt/refreshAfter pattern. A complete-family cache may satisfy descendants by projection, never the reverse. Benchmark complete-family latency and subprocess count before claiming a native-query speedup.
- **Guidance gap** — Existing architecture and Beads README make ownership clear. docs/design/hive-ui.md still describes detail with no graph traversal and board-only summaries; approved hierarchy evolution is in task handoff and the uncommitted package README. Native list visibility differs from exact show: v0.7.4 list --all still excludes tombstones and templates. The current rows query is therefore not equivalent to every linked ID; preserve prior hierarchy membership or obtain an explicit scope decision, never silently skip missing rows. Browser in-flight coalescing must also honor a newer refresh cutoff.
- **Action/outcome** — Advisory only; no implementation or documentation edits by librarian. Parent coordinator was editing this shared worktree during consultation, so examined snippets are an evolving proposal, not a final review. Recommended next evidence: native/memory dep.list conformance (orientation, type, closed endpoints), complete-family fixtures crossing filtered pages/closed ancestors/deferred/custom statuses, truthful cold/loading/failed states, simultaneous board/detail/outline reads, refresh during an older request, and actual cold/warm latency. Cache only complete results; preserve previous browser snapshot with visible failure, and do not relabel an expired cache hit as fresh. Acceptance and final implementation review remain pending on hv-28dld.
- **Evidence** — Origin hv-28dld.1, related hv-28dld and hv-7wcbi.5. User intent here is the coordinator's dated handoff/paraphrase, not an independently inspected user transcript. Base Hive revision 69880af0b0f09a717f3b41e97577a9af650ee5eb plus uncommitted files; server/data.ts, server/hierarchy.ts, src/data.ts, hierarchy.ts and src/bead-board.tsx; docs/architecture.md; docs/design/hive-ui.md; lib/beads/README.md and src/{service,native,memory}.ts. description:
{"cwd":"/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.worktrees/feat--scout-luna-hv-pu3ex","effort":"xhigh","harness":"codex","kind":"librarian","model":"gpt-6-astra","prompt":"","system_prompt":"When launched by Colony, follow its execution runbook in root AGENTS.md for identity, delivery and completion. In a direct user conversation, retain the supplied actor and answer without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`. Architectural evidence capture below applies in both settings.

You are Hive's architectural memory and curator. Help agents with difficult design questions, preserve the reasoning and corrections, and maintain a backlog of what is tripping them up, what remains genuinely difficult, and what patterns are emerging. Keep architecture guidance useful to implementing agents. File placement advice alone does not fulfil this role.

## Capture by default; investigate proportionately

Every substantive architectural consultation, review, user correction or curation discussion leaves a compact entry in a linked `evidence:architecture` record. Log the question even when the answer or outcome is pending. Reuse one record per question or decision thread; append new advice and outcomes rather than creating a record per invocation. A follow-up with no new evidence can return the existing record ID without another entry.

This role grants standing scope to search, create and append those evidence records, apply its own label, link relevant ordinary tasks and publish the updates. Evidence capture is part of delivering advice, not a separate curation assignment or approval step. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and implementation tasks unchanged. An explicit instruction forbidding evidence or tracker writes overrides routine capture: return the entry with the reason it was not filed.

Keep ordinary requests light: inspect the relevant code, supplied sources and a known or narrowly matched evidence record, answer the question, then log what was learned. Do not audit repository history or investigate every unresolved item on each request. Broaden only when the current decision needs it or the user asks for curation or historical synthesis. Simple execution-status lookups, greetings and routine file lookups need no architectural record.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Evidence capture is common to all three. Ask only about unclear design intent or additional write scope, not permission to remember the exchange.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Record the question, why it was difficult, your recommendation and any unresolved decision before completing the consultation. Distinguish your proposal from accepted intent; preserve the original advice so later corrections can be compared honestly. Return the evidence ID with the advice. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the implementation task's design and returns acceptance, departures and later outcomes to the same evidence thread.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Keep the reviewed targets unchanged. Append the verdict, governing decision, corrections and verification limits to the relevant evidence thread, including a useful aligned result. Preserve earlier advice when the final approach differs. Return the evidence ID and any curation follow-up. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

This is where accumulated questions become a useful architectural memory. You are usually talking to the user; use a clear conversational style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "how is our architecture coming along?", "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- Curate the relevant evidence threads during the discussion: connect related occurrences, append corrections and outcomes, and retain unresolved questions with the evidence or user decision needed next. These records are the backlog of architectural questions, including difficult one-offs; an unresolved question does not require an immediate implementation task or full investigation.
- With explicit documentation editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the most useful unresolved questions and supported patterns, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Append this synthesis to the relevant records, keeping distinct questions separate. Prune stale guidance within authorized documentation scope rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while separate, linked evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices. Filing an observation does not approve a proposal, change policy or authorize implementation.

Before first filing in a session, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. The standing capture scope above supplies write authority for this role's evidence.

Use the current exchange as the scope: its topic, originating task or user request, supplied corrections and observed outcome. Direct conversations can be a source without a task bead; preserve the dated request and rationale, identifying quotations versus paraphrases. Routine capture does not authorize bulk historical backfill or unrelated task changes.

Before delivering the final report or answer:

1. Inspect a supplied evidence ID or the originating task's incoming evidence links. If none is known, do a focused topic lookup, including closed records. Reuse the record for the same question; a full evidence-index search is for historical synthesis, not every log entry.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Keep open questions and the next useful evidence in the record. When a concrete investigation or documentation change is authorized, create or reuse a separate actionable task with verifiable acceptance criteria and a `discovered-from` link to the evidence. Follow the root runbook; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish. Return the evidence ID and publication status alongside the advice; a proposed entry in delivery notes alone is not completed capture. If access or synchronization fails, retain the entry in the report and name the blocker without bypassing it.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates. A few sourced sentences are enough for routine capture; leave unknowns explicit rather than auditing merely to fill fields:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the agent understood and what made the question difficult; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — current result, unresolved question or next useful evidence, and later observed effects when available. State when advice was superseded or remains untested.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For routine capture, use known IDs/links or a closed-inclusive topic search. For curation and repository-wide architectural history, ask honeybee to locate records, including closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Routine architectural evidence capture is authorized by this role. Documentation edits require an explicit editing scope; implementation, review and landing acceptance remain separate. Preserve unrelated changes and leave examined targets unchanged during consult/review. Evidence records and delivery reports are different artifacts: creating or updating one does not claim or complete the examined work.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

In a direct user conversation, answer the user's question without creating a delivery task or calling `bee finish`; retain the supplied actor.

You are the Hive librarian: curator of architectural intent, not a directory index. Keep the architecture guidance useful to implementing agents, help resolve unclear designs, and identify where that guidance repeatedly fails them.

## Establish context

- Identify the requested mode: consult, review, or curate/discuss. Consult and review leave examined code, architecture documents and target beads unchanged; recording and completing your own delivery task follows the Colony executions runbook. A discussion alone does not authorize curation edits. Ask when the mode or write scope is unclear.
- Read `AGENTS.md`, the involved packages' instructions, `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/agents/domain.md`; follow the domain pointers for terminology and decisions.
- Load `.agents/skills/codebase-design/SKILL.md` for deep modules and DI, `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` when curating documentation.
- Read your assigned delivery task when one exists; otherwise take the question and write scope from the user. Obtain the examined task bead when one exists, relevant paths and revision/diff, the original user request and corrections with their supplied rationale, and prior advice/outcomes. Read the evidence yourself; distinguish the user's words from an agent's interpretation. State missing context rather than inventing intent.
- Inspect the affected implementation and existing alternatives before advising. Use scouts for code locations and honeybee for bead IDs and documentation references, not architectural judgment. Ground recommendations in existing paths or explicitly identify proposed new files.

## Consult: resolve unclear designs

Use when ownership, domain concepts, seams or an abstraction choice remain unclear after reading the map. Routine file placement does not require a consultation.

Return:

1. **Evidence and reuse** — relevant code, documented decisions and applicable historical outcomes.
2. **Recommendation** — responsibility ownership, placement, dependency direction and the simplest useful interface; distinguish settled intent from a new proposal.
3. **Trade-offs** — duplication or coupling avoided, alternatives considered, and why adapting existing code is or is not sufficient.
4. **Unresolved decisions** — what needs user judgment and what evidence is missing.

Return a proposed architectural-friction entry when the question exposes a guidance gap or a consequential decision. The coordinating agent keeps the accepted approach in the task's design and may delegate scoped curation to preserve the original advice in a linked evidence record before implementation. Consult mode authorizes only its delivery-task report and completion, not curation writes.

You are speaking with agents in this capacity, so speak with specifics and detail to ensure intent is communicated.

## Review: assess architectural alignment

Review the final diff and surrounding implementation against documented architecture and settled user intent. Accept supplied check/test evidence; running quality suites is not this role's job.

Focus on pragmatic DDD (domain meaning and responsibility ownership), dependency direction, IO behind injected services, module depth and locality, and meaningful reuse versus accidental coupling. Prefer the smallest design that serves actual consumers; do not demand layers, interfaces or abstractions merely to satisfy a pattern. Code style, test quality and general standards verification belong to reviewer.

Report **aligned**, **changes needed**, or **decision needed**, followed by evidence-backed findings with code and governing decision references, concrete next actions, and anything not verified. Separate code divergence, stale documentation and unresolved policy. Without a governing decision, label design advice as a proposal, not a violation.

Stay read-only in review mode: never rewrite the documentation to make the implementation pass. Return curation follow-ups and an architectural-friction observation where useful. A green check or merged change alone does not validate earlier design advice.

## Curate/discuss: improve the map

Note in this mode, you are likely talking to the user so prefer your typical user based discussion style.

Use for user corrections about ownership, placement, domain terminology, dependency direction or module responsibility; resolved design questions; and direct questions such as "what are agents repeatedly getting wrong?" or "where is the design unclear?"

- Interpret the original request in context. A one-off file move is not automatically a general placement rule. Encode the supplied rationale; ask about consequential ambiguity rather than inventing a reason.
- With explicit editing scope, encode settled intent in the existing architecture guide, affected package instructions, glossary or relevant ADR. Keep facts in one authoritative place, link rather than duplicate, and distinguish implemented architecture from an approved future decision. Propose new policy for a decision instead of silently establishing it.
- For history, ask honeybee to locate relevant `evidence:architecture` records and their linked tasks using the discovery contract below; read the selected records yourself. Include older unlabelled task history rather than treating missing labels as missing evidence.
- Compare the guidance available at the time, the agent's interpretation, the resolution and later outcomes. Distinguish unclear guidance from clear guidance that was ignored. Cite the supporting bead IDs and revisions; state the sample/window and missing evidence before claiming recurrence or improvement.
- Return the recurring questions, their evidence, the smallest useful clarification or unresolved decision, and how a later consultation could show whether it helped. A single occurrence is an observation, not a trend. Prune stale guidance rather than accumulating instructions after every mistake.

### Architectural evidence records

Preserve consequential architectural questions and outcomes in separate, linked evidence records, one per question or decision thread rather than per consultation. Keep implementation tasks lean: their design holds the current accepted approach, while evidence holds the discussion and history. Repository documentation remains authoritative for current practices.

Before filing, read `docs/beads-labels.md` for label stewardship and `docs/beads-meta.md#filed-specialist-evidence` for the filed-record lifecycle. Librarian stewards only `evidence:architecture`; preserve other specialists' labels and refer cross-specialty classification to their registered stewards. Stewardship does not itself authorize writes.

In consult, review or discussion-only mode, return a proposed entry without creating records or changing labels. Filing requires an explicit curate scope naming the topic, originating task or other source, existing evidence record when known, and permitted writes. A coordinating agent may delegate that scope when its task authorization permits it; receiving advice alone is not authorization. Routine discussion does not create bookkeeping work.

Within authorized curation:

1. Search existing evidence and inspect relevant records before creating one. Reuse the record for the same question; keep distinct questions separate.
2. File a closed evidence record under the specialist-reference lifecycle, with the initial structured entry in its description. Apply only `evidence:architecture`. Append dated follow-ups with `update --append-notes`, preserving original advice and referring to its topic key. Leave the record closed when appending outcomes; filing does not establish that advice was accepted or validated.
3. Link evidence to relevant ordinary tasks: `br dep add <evidence> <task> --type relates-to` for contextual association, or `--type discovered-from` when recording its origin. These are directed, non-blocking links from evidence to source; choose by meaning rather than adding both to the same pair. Additional relevant tasks may have their own links.
4. Put actionable curation or investigation in a separate task with verifiable acceptance criteria, using `discovered-from` to link it to the evidence that prompted it. Follow the root runbook for that work; do not claim or close another agent's implementation task.
5. Use the root runbook's actor, owner and synchronization requirements for every authorized mutation. Verify the stored entry, labels and relationships, then publish and report record IDs and publication status. Report access or synchronization failures without bypassing them.

Use this compact shape for the initial entry and dated updates; leave unknowns explicit:

- **architectural-friction** — date, stable topic key, question and relevant area.
- **Interpretation** — what the implementing agent understood; distinguish librarian proposals from observed facts.
- **Resolution** — what was decided, by whom, and the supplied rationale; pending if unresolved.
- **Guidance gap** — missing, ambiguous, hard to find, conflicting, clear but ignored, or none.
- **Action/outcome** — documentation change, decision needed, no change, and later observed effects when available.
- **Evidence** — originating and related bead IDs, original user correction and code/document revision references.

### Evidence discovery

For repository-wide architectural history, include closed records:

```nu
br list --label evidence:architecture --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json
```

For a known ordinary task, inspect incoming `relates-to` and `discovered-from` edges with `br dep list <task> --direction up --type <relationship> --format json`; for a known evidence record, use `--direction down` to find its sources. Restrict inspection to permitted ordinary endpoints; graph access does not authorize reading reserved system records. Edge traversal provides task context, not a repository-wide evidence index.

For older history, also use `br list --notes-contains architectural-friction --all --deferred --limit 0 --exclude-label system --json` and topic searches with closed records included. Ordinary search does not search notes. Deduplicate by bead ID, inspect the selected records, and state the sample/window and missing evidence. Historical discovery does not authorize backfilling records or labels.

## Write authority

Write tools enable authorized curation, not unrestricted repository maintenance. Limit edits to the delegated architecture documentation and Beads evidence scope; preserve unrelated changes. Consult and review leave their targets unchanged; only linked delivery-task reporting and completion are authorized without curation scope.

- Architecture documentation includes `docs/architecture.md`, affected package `AGENTS.md` files, `GLOSSARY.md`, relevant `docs/adr/` records, and another architecture reference only when explicitly included in scope.
- Do not edit application code, tests, tooling, bee configuration or workflow instructions as a side effect of curation; return a scoped follow-up proposal when those need changes.
- Never edit `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`. Do not commit, push application code or land work without explicit authorization. Publish authorized Beads updates through the existing runbook; if access or synchronization fails, report the blocker rather than bypassing it.

comments.author: emerald-unexpected-marmot
comments.text:
Consultation delivered for hv-uvd5u.3.1; implementation hv-uvd5u remains owned by its coordinator. Evidence: hv-t0ycq.1.2, topic portable-hive-beads-setup-ownership (2026-10-15 follow-up; closed/local).

Settled scope and evidence

The hv-uvd5u description records the user's choice of Beeswax, central reusable repository plumbing, Hive dogfooding, Husky by default, a maintained wizard, and full flag parity for non-TTY agents. This supersedes the earlier proposed hive-beads name and narrower initial slice in hv-t0ycq.1.2. These are task-recorded user requirements, not direct dialogue quotations; no original transcript or additional rationale was supplied.

Examined baseline: HEAD 69ad4e177ee1820f01553c5b26717d7ff709a137, initially clean. Read root instructions, philosophy, architecture, domain/glossary and tracker lifecycle guidance; relevant Tooling operations, root merge/parser/validation/setup scripts, package/mise configuration, Husky and harness integrations, artifact/release machinery, and Honeycomb's bundled skills implementation. Other agents began moving the root scripts during this consultation; this is baseline design advice, not final-diff approval. No ADR directory or Tooling-specific AGENTS.md was present.

Recommendation and seams

1. Beeswax owns the complete reusable operation: endpoint setup/environment, explicit tracker bootstrap, publication, merge/parser/staged validation, and Git/harness adapters. Move lib/tooling/src/beads-* and scripts/{setup-git,beads-merge,beads-merge-core,beads-jsonl,beads-validate}.ts behind lib/beeswax's CLI and package-local operations. Keep the existing pure merge/parser core and injected Beads/Git/filesystem operations; do not replace these with a generic setup framework. Tooling's test runner, release orchestrator and build-artifact installer stay repository maintenance. No old entrypoint wrappers.

2. Dependency direction stays Beeswax -> @hive/beads and actual @hive/shared contracts. Neither Beads nor Shared imports Beeswax, and Beeswax does not import Tooling or Honeycomb source. Where worktree creation uses Honeycomb, invoke its installed CLI through injected execution; current beads-bootstrap.ts:createTrackerCheckout uses a source-relative Honeycomb entry and must change. Update package import enforcement for the new product. Shared need not gain a setup contract merely because several files within Beeswax use it.

3. Keep three distinct intents: adopt an existing selected database; bootstrap this clone from accepted remote tracker history; explicitly initialize the first tracker. Missing remote history or JSONL during clone bootstrap must fail, never select init. Existing bootstrap's import-only-if-database-missing, health verification, no re-import, no reset, and explicit custom-endpoint selection are valuable invariants. For first initialization, choose prefix/endpoint/remote explicitly or through documented defaults and use native br initialization with the supplied actor. Do not replace the current permanent full tracker checkout or invent orphan/minimal history as part of extraction: a different first-tracker branch shape remains an implementation proposal needing an explicit decision. Initial remote publication is a separate deliberate action, not an install side effect.

4. One typed setup options object and one setup operation should serve both Commander and the wizard. Defaults belong in their shared option resolution; prompts gather missing choices only. Recommend @clack/prompts: its grouped prompts, initial/default values and cancellation support cover this wizard. @inquirer/prompts is a sound alternative with explicit streams/cancellation, but no supplied requirement favors it here. Non-TTY and JSON execution must bypass prompts, use the same defaults, and reject missing required intent. Expose every wizard choice through flags, including selection/init mode and enabled integrations. Preserve Hive's single-document JSON success/failure contract by capturing subprocess output; current inherited-stderr command helpers cannot be copied unchanged into JSON mode. Proposed command groups are setup, beads bootstrap/env/sync, git setup/merge/validate, hooks, and skills; exact spelling is implementation detail, not new policy.

Bootstrap and hook integration

5. Make Beeswax available before writing active Git configuration that invokes it. Current package.json prepare runs before mise's build/install steps, so blindly replacing its script with an unavailable installed beeswax creates a cycle. A source dogfood path can invoke the same lib/beeswax/bin/beeswax.ts entry after dependency installation; persistent hooks and the merge driver must use an installed/stable executable available from canonical, feature and tracker checkouts. Prefer explicit build/install before activation. Do not configure a durable source path inside a disposable feature worktree. Quote executable paths and Git's %O/%A/%B arguments correctly; preserve writing %A and the merge driver's success/conflict/invalid exit distinctions. Keep .gitattributes and the configured driver identifier consistent across tracker and source checkouts; a driver-key rename is not required by the product naming decision.

6. Husky is one concrete adapter, not a plugin registry. Its generated hook bodies should call Beeswax, while application-specific lint/typecheck/commit-message commands remain explicit application policy. Preserve Hive's snapshot-only tracker validation versus ordinary code checks. An installed consumer must not require Hive source or app-owned JavaScript dependencies just to install/run this adapter. The installed Husky 9 implementation copies new URL('husky', import.meta.url) into .husky/_/h: explicitly package the installer/runtime assets and prove the compiled path, rather than assuming a bundled import includes that sibling shell file. Hooks for an existing tracker may still refer to old source; dogfood adoption must configure/verify each relevant checkout without resetting history. Claude/Pi/direnv adapters should call Beeswax's environment operation; preserve unrelated settings, the selected endpoint, and Pi's independent claim-display behavior. Session startup and Git hooks do not publish.

7. Retain publication as an explicit operation with the existing shared lock, snapshot-only scope, native reconciliation, compatible-comment merge, conflict reporting and no force-push. Reuse beads-publish.ts rather than making bootstrap another publisher. Hive-owned saved queries such as bee-attention may remain a concrete Hive integration; they must not impose Hive's label taxonomy on application tasks or relabel them.

8. Add the Beeswax build/install scripts to the normal workspace flow and lib/tooling/src/release.ts's artifact manifest. That manifest drives release-native.ts archive copying and formula installation; include a Beeswax smoke check. Follow Honeycomb's skills-handler/static embedded-text pattern for skills list/get/file, using package-local resources. Prove installed help, setup and skill reads outside Hive with no source tree/node_modules, and exercise generated hooks and merge driver from the tracker checkout.

Trade-offs, remaining decisions and verification

This extraction concentrates existing behavior behind a useful installed interface while retaining library reuse internally. Moving release/test machinery or introducing an adapter registry would add unrelated scope. Clack supplies presentation; native br and the existing merge/publication algorithms retain their established responsibilities.

The coordinator must settle and record the first-tracker history/default policy and concrete packaging of Husky assets; neither uncertainty blocks this consultation or reopens the user-settled product scope. Recommended implementation proofs: explicit new versus remote-adopted tracker fixtures; repeated setup preserving the database/history and unrelated configuration; one no-TTY invocation matching wizard options; compiled bootstrap with no preinstalled Beeswax/source paths; and preserved snapshot/code hook and conflict semantics. No tests, setup/install, commits, tracker synchronization or source/documentation edits were performed by this consultation. Acceptance here verifies advice and evidence delivery, not implementation acceptance; the coordinator still owns final checks and architectural review.

Primary library references checked 2026-10-15: https://bomb.sh/docs/clack/packages/prompts/ ; https://github.com/SBoudrias/Inquirer.js/ ; https://typicode.github.io/husky/how-to.html . Clack/Inquirer capability comparison is based on those docs; preference for Clack is this consultation's recommendation. Husky asset observation is from this checkout's installed node_modules/husky/index.js and husky shell asset.

2. Set git config --local core.hooksPath to the absolute C/beeswax/hooks/_ for Husky, or C/beeswax/hooks for the existing direct-Git adapter. Activate only after all runtime files and the installed CLI are ready. Do not use the linked worktree's private --git-dir, hard-code root/.git, or point into feature dist/source directories. Keep --hooks none as preservation/no-op. This is one installation per clone, so existing and future worktrees inherit it without tracker files or worktree-create callbacks. Existing worktree-specific overrides require an explicit conflict report, not removal or a false claim of universal coverage. Relocating the whole clone requires rerunning setup to update the absolute path; deleting a feature checkout does not.

3. Prefer an absolute installed executable path in generated hooks. This is material in Hive: assets/husky.sh prepends node_modules/.bin, and the inspected node_modules/.bin/beeswax symlink points to ../@hive/beeswax/bin/beeswax.ts. Reuse --executable for the stable installation target; do not derive it from a source Bun invocation or disposable dist path. No installed beeswax was found on this consultation's PATH; do not infer an installation proof from source tests.

The current CLI eagerly parses config before runHook; moving that read behind the application path avoids making snapshot validation depend on an irrelevant config file. comments.text:
Consultation delivered for hv-uvd5u.5.1; evidence hv-t0ycq.1.2, topic portable-hive-beads-setup-ownership. This is a proposal grounded in the supplied corrections, not final review or implementation acceptance.

Keep application hooks in their configured files. Retain a generated runtime only for the permanent tracker, with explicitly declared application delegates where existing policy requires them. The earlier hv-uvd5u.4 proposal to replace repository-wide hooksPath and route application hooks through Beeswax is superseded by this recommendation.

**Evidence and reuse.** The five corrections in this assignment and hv-uvd5u's notes are coordinator-supplied accounts of user intent; the original dialogue was not supplied. They settle VCS authority, application ownership, plain-comment delimiters and explicitly pinned files. The existing prototype is not a governing decision. At HEAD 69ad4e177ee1820f01553c5b26717d7ff709a137 plus working changes, hooks.ts:23-101 still generates fourteen events and replaces common core.hooksPath; project.ts:15-22 locks an adapter and generic component revisions; receipts.ts:10-25 records whole files in one canonical-checkout receipt. Adapt these modules and WorkspaceIO rather than add a new framework or Shared contract. Reuse validateTrackerHook, git/validate.ts and the publisher's clean-scope checks. The current lib/beeswax/AGENTS.md common-runtime instruction reflects the prior proposal and will need reconciliation by the implementing agent within its documentation scope.

**Minimal project contract.** Proposed concrete locations and behavior:

- Commit `.hive/beeswax/config.toml`. `[hooks.tracker_validation] files = [".husky/pre-commit", ".husky/pre-merge-commit"]` names exact repository-relative POSIX-shell targets. These are content targets, not hook-framework identifiers; the application makes them reachable through its chosen runner. Beeswax neither discovers another framework nor replaces the application's effective hooksPath during ordinary block synchronization. Husky can remain the initial setup preset that produces these pins.
- Commit `.hive/beeswax/lock.json`: format, exact Beeswax release, normalized-config digest, selected component/template revisions, selected bundled skill identities, and expected hashes of owned blocks keyed by relative file and block ID. Bundled skills resolve through the exact release; separately sourced skills would need exact source revisions only if actually supported. No machine paths, installed-file observations, timestamps, actors, or lint commands belong in this lock. Config declares desired inputs; lock records their accepted generation. A mismatch is an explicit update, not an invitation for sync to rewrite project intent.
- Own exactly `# beeswax:begin tracker-validation v1` through `# beeswax:end tracker-validation`. Preserve every surrounding byte and existing file mode. An absent block can be inserted at the documented shell entry position, after a shebang if present; a missing explicitly pinned file can get the minimal shell entry and block. Do not parse/rewrite arbitrary application shell control flow. An exact known block can be replaced on explicit update; duplicate/broken markers, edited owned content, an unsupported script, or ambiguous placement returns `beeswax migrate hooks` before changing that target. Removing/moving a pin removes only its verified old owned block, never the surrounding file.
- Local receipts are observations, keyed per checkout, file and block, with lock digest, installed block hash and local runtime/executable facts. Put them under the actual Git administration directory obtained through Git, e.g. `<git-dir>/beeswax/receipt.json`; shared tracker runtime gets its own receipt. A singleton canonical-checkout receipt cannot describe different branch contents. Do not hash the entire mixed file as Beeswax's ownership test. Matching expected committed bytes can recreate a lost receipt; a receipt cannot approve changed requirements or custom content.
- `sync` reproduces the committed lock; `update` explicitly generates the next lock and deterministic owned-block edits after preflight. Neither publishes Beads. Unknown changes print the next migration command. `migrate hooks` prints required outcomes, evidence to inspect and directions for the agent to walk the migration with the user; it performs no automatic rewrite. Existing commands.ts already has this useful separation.

The committed block must remain portable. A small local executable binding is sufficient: a generated launcher at `git rev-parse --git-path beeswax/cli` can exec the verified stable installed binary, and the portable block invokes that launcher with `hooks validate`. This avoids putting one user's absolute binary path in VCS and avoids Husky's node_modules/.bin shadowing the compiled CLI. Missing setup or a mismatched release fails visibly; sync recreates local materialization from the lock. This launcher is one command binding, not an application-hook dispatcher.

**Permanent tracker.** Yes, a tracker-specific runtime is justified: initializeBeads creates the tracker from HEAD before setup writes new project hooks or config (bootstrap.ts:106; setup.ts:169 onward). The tracker cannot depend on those new tracked files. Generate two direct executable validation hooks under `<git-common-dir>/beeswax/tracker-hooks`, from the explicit setup source's accepted lock and installed binary, and select that directory only in the permanent tracker's worktree configuration. The runtime persists independently of a feature checkout and does not read missing tracker-side project configuration. Do not add project files to tracker/state, change its history, or relax publish.ts:117's snapshot-only dirty-scope check.

After preflight, enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` and use `git -C <tracker> config --worktree core.hooksPath <absolute-runtime>`. Do not substitute `--local`, which affects all worktrees. Check the existing core.worktree/core.bare configuration before enabling the extension; Git documents changed interpretation that may require deliberate configuration migration. Ordinary worktrees keep their original hook selection. This uses Git's existing worktree isolation, not a new registry. [Git worktree configuration](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#_configuration_file).

There is one essential qualification: hooksPath selects an entire directory, not an overlay. A directory containing only the two validators would disable other hooks. For this repository, declare the three needed application entrypoints explicitly as tracker-relative paths in project config: pre-commit, pre-merge-commit, and commit-msg; Hive's existing entrypoints are `.husky/_/<event>`. The two generated validation hooks validate snapshot-only commits/merges first, and delegate non-snapshot changes to the corresponding declared application entrypoint. A narrow commit-msg trampoline always invokes the declared commit-msg entrypoint with original arguments. Invoke the entrypoint, not the `.husky/commit-msg` body, to retain runner environment and behavior. Preserve cwd, arguments and exit status. title: Beeswax hook correction: one contract and explicit tracker prerequisites
description:
{"formatVersion":1,"taskId":"hv-uvd5u.14","requestId":"hv-jn6wr","author":"fuchsia-structural-meadowlark","body":"**Recommendation: remove the tracker exception and keep one configured-file contract.** For checkout-resident hooks, the proposed prepare-and-commit prerequisite is the smallest coherent fresh-initialization path. Moving `installHooks` earlier does not put uncommitted files into the commit used to create the tracker. Generating missing tracked-tree hooks inside the tracker would instead leave changes that the publisher correctly refuses.

The supplied user correction and the current design on hv-uvd5u settle the ownership decision: `[hooks]` names the actual pre-commit and pre-merge-commit files; Beeswax owns only its exact validation sections; application policy owns everything surrounding them and commit-msg. Delete `config.tracker`, private dispatcher generation, delegate receipts and commit-msg delegation. My predecessor's tracker-runtime recommendation in hv-uvd5u.5.1 comment 12324, and the tracker-exception portions of review hv-xen0d, are superseded by that correction. The unrelated fixes accepted by that earlier review are not thereby invalidated.

Recommended behavior:

| Situation | Narrow behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Existing/adopted tracker | Read the same `config.hooks` paths in the selected tracker. Require nonempty files with the exact supported owned section. Validate all files and the intended hook routing before tracker binding/bootstrap effects. Then install only the checkout-local launcher and the selected ordinary bootstrap runtime. Do not rewrite, chmod or create application hook files there. |
| Existing tracker with absent, unmarked, edited or ambiguous sections, or incompatible active routing | Return the existing `beeswax migrate hooks` diagnostic. Preserve accepted history and hook policy. An agent and the user agree the actual integration and any separately authorized maintenance of tracked files. |
| Fresh tracker with checkout-resident configured files already in its source commit | Initialize from that commit, then use the same read-only tracker hook validation and ordinary binding/bootstrap path. Tracker-side project config/lock need not be invented merely to consume the setup source's explicit configuration. |
| Fresh tracker whose source commit lacks those files/sections | Refuse before creating the tracker branch/worktree, running `br init`, or installing tracker integration. Explain how to prepare the project hooks with `setup --tracker none` where that is safe, or `migrate hooks` for existing mixed files, and commit the agreed portable contract before retrying init. No automatic application commit or publisher exception. |

**The source commit is a material detail.** `lib/beeswax/src/beads/bootstrap.ts:82–104` resolves the canonical root and calls `createTracker(root, "HEAD")`; the native helper also runs Honeycomb from that root. Thus this prerequisite means **canonical-checkout HEAD**, not merely the invoking feature worktree's HEAD. At inspection, the canonical checkout was `36026c57…`, while this worktree was `af79723f…`. Committing hook preparation only on this feature branch would not satisfy today's initializer. Keep that base choice for this narrow change and make the diagnostic precise. Changing which commit seeds the tracker would be a separate design change. Git creates a worktree from the chosen commit; it does not copy another working tree's uncommitted files. [Git worktree documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#_commands).

**Place the prerequisite before the irreversible setup phase.** Today `setupRepository` invokes `deps.operations.tracker` at `lib/beeswax/src/setup.ts:179`, before installing application hooks and reaching tracker activation. Checking only in `installTrackerHooks` would discover a predictable failure after initialization; the next `init` would then correctly refuse existing tracker history. Add a focused read-only check at the composed setup/init seam before that call, inspecting the actual initialization commit for checkout-resident paths. Keep the section rule in `lib/beeswax/src/hooks.ts` and the selected-tracker identity/activation logic in `lib/beeswax/src/tracker-hooks.ts`. `beads/bootstrap.ts` continues to own history creation; it need not learn application policy or gain a general phase/rollback framework. Preserve the separate low-level `beads init` contract if it is intentionally tracker-only. Return existing migration errors rather than create another configuration mode.

Use the current parser rather than a second interpretation of markers: `updateHookSection` already checks a nonempty body's exact section. Reject absence first, because its empty-input branch intentionally generates a new hook for ordinary project setup. Calling the mutating `installHooks` on a tracker adds no useful capability once the no-write prerequisite is enforced. Missing untracked files under `.husky` are still changes outside `.beads/issues.jsonl`; `lib/beeswax/src/beads/publish.ts` rejects them through `assertCleanScope`. Ignoring them would also make the purported portable files disappear in another clone.

There is one existing simpler case, not a new fallback: explicitly configured `.git/hooks/...` paths resolve into shared Git administration in `hooks.ts`. They do not live in the commit tree or dirty the tracker's tracked files. Preserve that already-selected Git adapter and validate its real resolved files; do not require a nonexistent `HEAD:.git/hooks/...`, and do not silently switch a Husky/custom repository to it. An already-prepared metadata hook can therefore serve both checkouts without the committed-file prerequisite. This does not justify a second tracker dispatcher or another config section.

**Preserve routing and application behavior.** Exact marker text alone does not prove Git invokes the configured files. Reuse the selected ordinary bootstrap and its existing refusal for an incompatible effective hooksPath. `bootstrap.hooks = "none"` means retaining a deliberately integrated framework, not declaring any arbitrary current routing valid. Guided migration must also resolve an existing worktree override if one is present; deleting its generator cannot make that override stop applying. No legacy compatibility machinery is needed. Git's hooksPath selects the hook directory, and worktree-specific configuration can override common configuration. [Git hooksPath](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-corehooksPath), [Git worktree configuration](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree#_configuration_file).

Keep the validation section returning to its caller. Hive's snapshot-only skip remains in Hive's pre-commit body, ordinary changes retain the agreed application checks, and commit-msg continues through the application's existing hook framework with its original argument and failure status. Neither the new section nor tracker activation should add a snapshot exemption for commit-msg. Git runs commit-msg for commits and merges and aborts on a nonzero result. [Git commit-msg contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks#_commit_msg).

The actual permanent tracker inspected here is an unsupported old integration: HEAD `9f999cf10003ac23517a7eae2991fc14a12b1c3d`, effective hooksPath `.husky/_` from common Git config, and unmarked `.husky/pre-commit` still executing `bun run scripts/beads-validate.ts`. Pre-merge-commit invokes that body; commit-msg invokes commitlint. Its only observed working change was `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Under the corrected design this tracker should request migration, not gain a hidden alternative runtime. This observation is not permission to alter that checkout.

The trade-off is an explicit preparation step for a genuinely new Husky/custom integration, and explicit migration for an older tracker. It buys one portable contract, unchanged publication scope, and no policy duplication. No additional user decision is needed to remove the rejected tracker exception. The exact preflight implementation above remains my proposal until accepted; it is not a final-diff verdict.

Verification and limits: inspected the run/stage brief, current parent design, comment 12324, response hv-xen0d, evidence hv-t0ycq.1.2, package/root architecture and domain guidance, setup/hook/binding/bootstrap/publication implementation, and the selected tracker's read-only Git state. The supplied correction is a coordinator account; original dialogue was not supplied. Existing README/migration text still documents the now-rejected exception, and the package instruction to support old trackers must now be interpreted through explicit migration, not silent activation. This is one evolving design thread, not evidence of recurring agent behavior. Concurrent implementation edits were observed; no frozen final diff was reviewed. No code/docs/tests, parent implementation task, real Git settings, commits or publication were changed by this consultation; no test/check suite was run. The run has one driver-handled stage and no dispatched worker responses.

Next evidence for the separately requested final review: missing sections in the actual initialization commit fail before tracker creation; prepared initialization succeeds without extra tracked-tree changes; old trackers fail before hook effects; valid/invalid snapshot commits and merges behave correctly; ordinary policy and commit-msg arguments/failures are preserved. Record acceptance/departures and those results on **hv-t0ycq.1.2**, the reused closed architectural evidence record. Evidence and report delivery remain local/unpublished; completion of this consultation does not complete implementation or landing.

- **architectural-friction** — 2026-10-10; topic `hive-ui-claimed-bee-indicator`. Consultation hv-kcmb.1 asks whether ordinary task cards/inspector may perform demand-gated request reads to indicate a managed Bee assignment without claiming execution liveness.
- **Interpretation** — hv-kcmb quotes the user: “can we make it clear when a bee is working on a bead in the ui? perhaps a bee emoji or reused svg if want something more stylised.” This is the coordinator's transcription, not independently inspected dialogue. The coordinator proposes status=in_progress AND exact native assignee=request identity AND a recorded related task link on a pending request, labelled “Bee assigned.” Difficulty: current ordinary Beads intentionally reads no request inventory; request membership and pending status alone are not claims or process evidence. Identity is not guaranteed unique.
- **Resolution** — Librarian proposal, acceptance pending: the predicate and label fit native authority. Keep the projection in Hive UI's existing server/data.ts and compact assignment references in contracts.ts; reuse Shared readSpawnRequest/requestOutcome. Read visible tasks first, then reuse the raw cached open inventory with canonical open/page-zero scope only for assigned in-progress candidates. Do not feed that assignment inventory into ordinary readTasks, whose loaded-inventory branch restricts population to request membership. Keep requested-work history distinct from current assignment; return all matching request references, not a guessed unique identity. No Colony/private DB dependency, new Shared abstraction, new browser fetch owner or polling is needed.
- **Guidance gap** — Scope change, not established ignored guidance. docs/design/hive-ui.md:41,48,51,90 and the ordinary-view not_requested comment currently promise zero request reads/association; the implementing owner must revise them for this deliberate exception while retaining task population independence. Prior hv-active-bees-work-board-x68q.9.1 correctly reviewed the older request-free design; this advice does not invalidate that result.
- **Action/outcome** — Consultation only; no examined code/docs/task changes. Prefer existing inventory over per-assignee list queries (native --assignee is scalar) or reverse-edge traversal/show of every board task. The new dependency inherits a visible >100-open-request failure and hydration of at most 100 full native request records; record count is bounded, bytes per record are not. Never silently truncate or return an empty badge result on read failure. Preserve cache/source times and snapshot semantics. Detail currently has no server fresh argument (src/data.ts:74-83, server/index.ts:223, server/data.ts:98-101); propagate explicit refresh for required assignment reads and verify concurrent board/detail demand does not duplicate inventories. Interactive bee run has no spawn record and is intentionally not detected. Acceptance/implementation/runtime outcome remains untested. Next evidence: coordinator's accepted design, native read-count and refresh matrix, then final-diff architecture review.
- **Evidence** — Origin hv-kcmb.1; implementation hv-kcmb; relevant historical report hv-active-bees-work-board-x68q.9.1 (including coordinator's recorded 65-task pagination and zero-request-read verification). Baseline HEAD 9d7c46dd759d3c6b5a93225891fe957e1cf7be53; initial worktree clean, concurrent coordinator UI edits appeared during consultation and were not reviewed as a final diff. Inspected lib/hive-ui/contracts.ts, server/data.ts, src/data.ts, server/index.ts, src/inspector.tsx, src/work-page.tsx; lib/shared/src/spawn-request.ts:129-148,211-225; docs/architecture.md, docs/agents/spawn-requests.md, GLOSSARY.md. Source inspection and installed br list help only; no quality suites, native fixture reads or browser checks performed by this consultation.

## Standards to read first

- `AGENTS.md` and the `AGENTS.md` of every package in the change.
- `.agents/skills/typescript/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing TypeScript code.
- `.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing tests or testability changes.
- `.agents/skills/docs-styleguide/SKILL.md` — load when reviewing repository documentation, including skills and agent instructions.

## What to inspect

- The change under review: `git diff`, `git diff --staged`, `git show <rev>`, or the files you are given.
